# Livewell Dental: Where Your Smile Inspires


A practice built around one patient at a time

Care that runs deeper than the immediate problem

A dentist who stays involved from first visit to final result


## We Believe Every Patient Deserves Dentistry Done at the Highest Level


Watch Now


## We Believe the Work We Do Here Has a Real Impact


Our team is here because this work means something to us. Dentistry changes more than teeth. It changes how someone eats, how they speaks, how they smiles, and how they carry themselves again. We see that every day, so every part of the experience matters to us, from the first conversation to the care we provide in the chair.

We are not trying to cover every specialty or serve every age group. Our focus is adult comprehensive care: restorative, cosmetic, and implant dentistry for people who want a result that lasts. That focus allows us to go deeper on every case rather than wider across every category.


## We Believe Consistency Builds the Kind of Trust That Takes Time


When you come to Livewell, you will always work with Dr. Chris. He plans your treatment, carries it out, and follows up on it. There is no associate you see on alternating visits, no junior provider who handles part of the case while Dr. Chris handles another. Every decision about your care runs through one person who knows your complete history.

That consistency matters more in dentistry than most patients realize. It means your bite analysis and your crown placement are understood by the same person. It means the notes from your last appointment are not just a file someone else skims before you sit down. It means continuity, and continuity means fewer mistakes.

Experience Dr. Chris' Care


### We Believe Advanced Dentistry Should Feel Straightforward


Dr. Chris trained at UCSF School of Dentistry, completed a residency in Advanced Education in General Dentistry, and continued his postgraduate education at the Kois Center in Seattle. He holds fellowship status with both the Academy of General Dentistry and the International Congress of Oral Implantologists, and he teaches implant dentistry to other clinicians across the country through the Implant Accelerator program.

Over 10 years of experience

UCSF School of Dentistry Graduate

AEGD Residency Completed at UCSF

Kois Center Graduate, Seattle WA

Fellow, Academy of General Dentistry (FAGD) — Top 6% of US Dentists

Fellow, International Congress of Oral Implantologists (FICOI)

Clinical Instructor, Implant Accelerator

Book Your First Visit


## WE BELIEVE YOUR COMFORT DURING TREATMENT IS NON-NEGOTIABLE, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT



### Preparation


We plan the visit before you arrive so treatment feels organized, predictable, and respectful of what you need to feel comfortable.


### Anesthesia


Dr. Chris cares deeply about this part, even practicing numbing techniques on himself early in his training, because comfort during treatment should never be guessed.


### Sedation


When anxiety or longer treatment needs more support, sedation can help make care feel calmer, safer, and more manageable.


### We Believe the Right Technology Produces Better Outcomes


Technology in dentistry is only useful when it improves what the clinician can see, plan, or deliver. We invest in equipment that meets that standard and nothing else.

Our 3D cone beam imaging lets us see bone structure, nerve pathways, and sinus anatomy in three dimensions before we plan any procedure. Our intraoral scanner captures a digital model of your teeth in minutes without the discomfort of traditional impressions. Our digital planning software lets us design your restoration before we prepare a single tooth. Our surgical guides, printed directly from scan data, help us place implants exactly where they were planned.

More About Our Technology


## We Believe the Details Matter Most


The gap between a good result and a great one is almost always in the details. The shade of a crown matched against natural light, not just a shade guide held up in a bright operatory. The contact between teeth that feels right on both sides, not just in one spot. The margin of a restoration that fits so precisely there is nowhere for bacteria to settle.


## See what our patients have to say.


We Believe Trust Comes From What Patients Experience, Not What We Say About Ourselves

STORIES OF THE LIVES WE’VE TOUCHED


### We Believe Treating the Cause Matters More Than Treating the Symptom


A lot of dentistry is reactive. Something hurts, something breaks, something falls out. A fix gets applied. Time passes. Something else happens. That cycle is expensive and exhausting, and it rarely moves your oral health in a better direction.

We approach every new patient with a full diagnostic review, not just a look at what is bothering them today. We want to understand the condition of every tooth, the health of the bone and tissue, how the bite is functioning, and what the risk factors are for future problems. That picture allows us to make recommendations that actually reduce your dental burden over time rather than adding to it appointment by appointment.

You see the same doctor every time, so your care does not feel rushed, random, or passed around.

You understand the plan before we begin, including what we see, what matters, and what each step is meant to solve.

Our recommendations are guided by evidence, experience, and judgment. Everything you need, nothing you don’t.

We handle complex care with confidence, and partner with trusted specialists when that is the better path.


### Reimagine your dental experience

# Meet the Livewell Dental Team


A small team built around trust, clarity, and thoughtful care.

Every person here plays a role in making your visit feel personal, calm, and well cared for.

From the first conversation to the final detail, our team is here to help your care feel connected.


## Meet the People Who Make Livewell Feel Like Livewell


At Livewell, great dentistry is not carried by one person alone. It takes a team that listens closely, communicates clearly, and notices the small details that make care feel calmer, more personal, and less overwhelming. From the first message to the final visit, our goal is simple: to help you feel seen, supported, and well cared for.


## Get to know our team



### Alejandra



#### OFFICE MANAGER


Hello and welcome to Livewell Dental! I have the pleasure of being the first face you'll see when you visit our clinic.

I was born and raised in El Salvador and have been living in the beautiful Lorton area since 2010. I am a huge fútbol fan (Hala Madrid!), love traveling and enjoy being outdoors/staying active.

Welcoming and assisting patients is something I'm truly passionate about. Working alongside Dr. Chris and the Livewell Dental team is an incredible experience, we share the same vision and passion for providing genuine care and support to our patients. Together, we strive to create a warm and welcoming environment, ensuring that each person who walks through our doors receives the best possible care and attention.

We can't wait to meet you!


### Amanda



#### Lead Clinical Assistant


Hello! I’m a dental assistant with a passion for the hands-on and creative aspects of dentistry. I love being part of a team that helps patients feel confident in their smiles while making their dental experience as comfortable and enjoyable as possible.

I enjoy traveling to see my favorite groups perform—BTS, Tomorrow X Together, and Seventeen. Experiencing their concerts in different places combines my love for music and adventure! At home, I spend my time with my loyal companion, Rambo—my amazing dog who keeps life exciting. I also have a deep love for traveling in general and hope to explore as much of the world as possible, experiencing new cultures and making unforgettable memories along the way.


### Cayla



#### DENTAL ASSISTANT


Hello! I’m Cayla, one of the dental assistants here at Livewell Dental.

I graduated from UVA with a degree in Cognitive Science, and I’m continuing my journey toward becoming a dentist.

What I love about dentistry is that it brings together so many things I care about: art, science, and the chance to connect with people in a meaningful way.

At the office, I enjoy getting to know our patients, helping them feel comfortable, and being part of the process that helps someone smile with more confidence.

Outside of dentistry, I love building LEGO sets, watching Formula 1, and oil painting.

I’m so excited to meet you and help make your experience here a great one.


### Robyn



#### DENTAL HYGIENIST


Hello! I’m Robyn, the dental hygienist here at Livewell Dental.

I graduated from Virginia Commonwealth University in 2013 and first joined Dr. Chris and the Livewell Dental team in 2021. After two years with the practice, my family moved overseas for a few years as part of military life. Now that we’re back in the area, I’m so happy to be back at Livewell and reconnecting with familiar faces while getting to know new ones.

One of my favorite parts of being a dental hygienist is building relationships with my patients. I want people to feel comfortable when they’re here, understand what’s happening with their oral health, and leave feeling like they have someone on their side. To me, great dental care is not just about taking care of teeth. It is about creating a positive experience and helping people build healthy habits they can carry with them for years.

Outside of the office, I’m a mom to two young children and two energetic dogs, so life stays pretty busy! I love traveling and spending time outdoors with my family, whether we’re hiking, exploring somewhere new, or spending a day at the beach. When I have some quiet time, I also love baking and crochet.

I’m grateful to be back with the Livewell Dental family and look forward to getting to know you and your family!


### Erica



#### Insurance Support Specialist


Hi! My name is Erica, and I'm an Insurance Support Specialist at Livewell Dental.

What I truly enjoy about working with Dr. Chris and the team is the constant opportunity to grow and discover new skills. I find immense satisfaction in building systems that help patients feel supported and ensure their appointments go smoothly. Contributing to something meaningful keeps me motivated and engaged every day.

Outside of work, I'm a big fan of K-pop idols—especially the group Seventeen—and I love getting lost in Korean movies and music. I also enjoy watching sunsets, being in high places where I can see mountains and city lights, and spending quality time with my family and friends. These peaceful moments help me recharge and stay grounded.

Above all, I believe in the power of positive communication and the importance of lifelong learning. I'm excited to be a part of your dental journey and look forward to helping make your experience with us smooth and stress-free!


### Kona



#### Office Mascot


Hi, my name is Kona, and I am the office mascot! Although you won't see me during business hours, I work off-hours to make sure every office corner is sparkly clean!

To look a part of being the mascot of a dental office, I brush my teeth daily and stay away from sweets. It's ruff!

When I am not busy working, I like to play fetch or take a stroll around Old Town Alexandria with my loving pawrents.


## More Than a Team


The best care comes from people who genuinely like being here, and it shows. These are the real moments between appointments: the laughs, the celebrations, the small kindnesses. It is who we are as a team, and it is what you feel the moment you walk in.

# The dCOE Experience at Livewell Dental


Addresses function, comfort, health, and aesthetics together

A clear plan built around your goals, needs, and timeline

Personally guided by Dr. Chris from diagnosis to next steps

Dr. Chris Explains Why Most Exams Miss the Full Picture

Watch Now


## Why Didn’t Anyone Ever Tell Me This Before?


Many dental visits focus on what is broken today, but not always on why it happened or how to keep the same problems from repeating. That can lead to frustrating repeat issues, surprise costs, and the feeling that you are always reacting instead of being in control.

We created the Dedicated Comprehensive Oral Evaluation, or dCOE, for patients who are ready to understand the full picture, especially those considering cosmetic dentistry, full smile makeovers, full mouth reconstruction, implants, or complex restorative care. Because lasting treatment begins with a clear diagnosis.


## How the dCOE Works


Two visits. Full records. A clear diagnosis before treatment begins.


### 1. ARRIVAL


DATA COLLECTION

Your first visit is focused on understanding your mouth, your history, and your goals. We take time for a detailed conversation, a functional and medical review, digital scans, X-rays or CBCT imaging when needed, and a comprehensive photo protocol that documents your teeth, bite, smile, and facial balance.

After this visit, Dr. Chris and the team study the records carefully before your second appointment. The goal is to understand what is happening, why it is happening, and what options make sense before any treatment is recommended.

Get Our Exclusive dCOE PDF


### 2. CONSULT


CASE PRESENTATION

At your second visit, you and Dr. Chris review your records together on screen. You will see your photos, scans, X-rays, bite findings, and any areas of concern in clear language.

From there, we discuss your current health, function, comfort, and aesthetics. If treatment is recommended, your plan includes the proposed sequence, estimated timeline, available options, and financial breakdown. The goal is for you to understand the “why” behind every recommendation before making a decision.


## From Dental Problems to a Smile That Feels Like Yours


A full-smile transformation is not just about changing teeth. It is about restoring comfort, confidence, function, and the freedom to smile without thinking about it.

Worn Edges

Uneven Smile Line

Discoloration

Old Dental Work

Bite Stress

Balanced Tooth Shape

Brighter Smile

Improved Smile Line

Natural Facial Fit

Better Bite Support


## The dCOE is perfect for you IF…


You have been told you need major dental work, but you do not fully understand why

You feel stuck in a cycle of failing dental work or repeated repairs

You want to fix the cause of the problem, not just patch it again

You are considering implants, cosmetic dentistry, or full mouth reconstruction and do not know where to start

You care about your long-term oral health, comfort, and function

You have wondered, “Why does this keep happening?” and want real answers


## Real Patients. Real Results.


view smile gallery

Read Patient Reviews


## A Practice That Stays Small to Focus Big On You


Dr. Chris leads each patient journey with intention, empathy, and advanced clinical training. As a Kois Center graduate, Fellow of the ICOI and AGD, and Clinical Instructor at Implant Accelerator, he brings comprehensive planning and careful documentation to complex cases at Livewell Dental.

Board-Level credentials

Fellowship training in implantology and general dentistry, the standard most patients with complex cases specifically look for.

Surgical Precision

Gum procedures most GPs refer out, performed in house by Dr. Chris.

One Patient at a Time

Your procedure is never rushed or competing with another appointment.

Fully Documented

Every case is photographed and measured from start to finish.


## Implant Experience That Extends Beyond the Practice


Dr. Chris is a Clinical Instructor at Implant Accelerator, where he helps other dentists develop their skills in implant planning and treatment. That teaching experience reflects the same principles behind the dCOE: diagnose carefully, document clearly, and plan treatment around the final result before treatment begins.


## From Dr. Chris


“The best dentistry should feel invisible. You shouldn’t have to think about it every day. That’s our goal—quietly excellent care that supports your health and fits into your life without distraction.”

Are there any must-do assessments before treatment (e.g., airway, bone volume)?

Before we begin any reconstructive treatment, we complete a comprehensive assessment—not just to plan the dentistry, but to understand why things have broken down in the first place. This step is non-negotiable because it’s how we ensure your treatment lasts and feels right for you.

Some of our must-do assessments include:

Airway & Breathing Evaluation

Your bite, jaw position, and even tooth wear can be influenced by how you breathe. We screen for airway issues that could be contributing to grinding, fatigue, or relapse after treatment.

Bone Structure & Volume (CBCT Scan)

We use 3D imaging to evaluate the health and density of your jawbone—especially critical if implants are part of the plan. It also helps us avoid vital structures like nerves and sinuses.

Functional Bite Analysis

Using tools like the Kois deprogrammer, we assess whether your muscles and joints are in harmony. Many patients have bite-related issues they’ve adapted to over time—this helps us identify and correct them before building on top.

Gum Health & Inflammation Screening

We can’t build on a foundation of inflammation. Healthy gums are essential for long-term success, and we use salivary diagnostics or bacterial testing when needed to guide treatment.

Photo & Digital Records

High-resolution photography, 3D scans, and models allow us to design your treatment with precision and transparency. You’ll see what we see—and be part of the decision-making process.

We don’t believe in rushing. We believe in clarity—because that’s what leads to confidence, comfort, and results that last.

Are there any clear disqualifiers (medical or psychological) we should mention?

We believe in doing the right thing for the right person at the right time. That means we’re not just looking at teeth—we’re looking at the whole person when deciding whether a reconstruction is appropriate.

While we welcome a wide range of patients, there are certain situations where full reconstruction may not be in someone’s best interest at this time. These may include:

Uncontrolled medical conditions — Certain systemic diseases (like poorly managed diabetes or autoimmune conditions) may delay healing or increase complication risks.

Severe untreated psychological conditions — For patients navigating significant anxiety, depression, body dysmorphia, or PTSD, we may recommend stabilization and support from other healthcare providers first. This ensures dental treatment is done in a healthy, sustainable context.

Unrealistic expectations — We’re here to restore health, function, and confidence—not create perfection. If someone is seeking a dramatic transformation without understanding the process, risks, or maintenance, we’ll take the time to pause and educate before proceeding.

Lack of commitment to follow-up care — Reconstructive dentistry requires a partnership. Without a willingness to maintain, protect, and monitor the work long-term, even the best dentistry will eventually fail.

None of these are judgments. They’re simply part of doing responsible, ethical dentistry. Our goal is always the same: to help you succeed—not just at the end of treatment, but for years to come.

Which tools should we highlight as part of your diagnostic and planning process?

To deliver care that lasts—and feels good long after you leave the chair—we invest heavily in diagnosis and planning. Here are just a few of the tools we use to help us understand your unique situation and design a solution that’s built to last:

Kois Deprogrammer

A custom-made bite appliance that allows your muscles to relax and reveal your true jaw position. This tells us if your bite is contributing to breakdown—and gives us a stable foundation before we build anything new.

Digital Intraoral Scanner

No goopy impressions here. Our scanner captures a 3D model of your teeth with high precision and comfort, helping us plan restorations with greater accuracy.

CBCT (3D X-ray Imaging)

Think of this as a 3D blueprint of your bone, nerves, and airway. We use it to plan surgeries, evaluate risk, and make decisions that protect both your health and longevity of your dental work.

High-Resolution Photography & Photo Studio

We document your smile in detail—both for communication and for smile design. This allows you to preview changes before we begin and helps us collaborate with our lab to achieve natural, lifelike results.

Digital Smile Design

Before we ever touch a tooth, you’ll be part of the process. We plan your new smile digitally, taking into account not just teeth—but your face, expressions, and personality.

These tools aren’t just about technology—they’re about intention. They give us clarity, precision, and a deeper understanding of what’s really going on—so your treatment is not just beautiful, but durable and aligned with your long-term health.

What’s the typical treatment length for most full-mouth cases?

Every full-mouth case is different—but what’s consistent is that we take our time to do things right.

Most full reconstructions are completed over 1 to 12 months, depending on the complexity. Some cases are faster, others take longer—especially if we’re including implants, gum therapy, or bite correction.

We typically break treatment into phases, which allows for healing, precision, and collaboration. It also gives you the chance to feel the changes step by step—and stay involved in the process.

The timeline depends on things like:

Whether we need to stabilize your bite or jaw joints first

If implants are involved (and need time to heal)

Whether there’s active disease or gum inflammation we need to treat first

Your availability and pace of decision-making

We’ll walk through the roadmap together, so you’ll always know where you are and what’s coming next. This isn’t cookie-cutter dentistry—it’s personal, thoughtful, and designed for long-term success.

Do you usually offer phased pricing (per quadrant or treatment stage)?

Yes—we do offer phased pricing when it’s appropriate.

In some cases, we can break treatment into quadrants or stages to help you move forward in a way that feels manageable—both clinically and financially. This approach works especially well when your case allows for it without compromising long-term results.

That said, we’re always careful to make sure phasing doesn’t mean compromising. Our priority is to treat the root cause, not just patch symptoms. So if breaking things up makes sense and still leads to a stable, predictable outcome, we’ll absolutely explore that with you.

Our commitment is simple: transparency, honesty, and a clear plan—so you always know what to expect, why we’re recommending something, and what the path forward looks like.

When do you recommend full-mouth implants, and when do you avoid them?

We don’t believe in one-size-fits-all solutions—especially when it comes to something as significant as full-mouth implants.

We may recommend full-mouth implant treatment when:

Teeth are no longer restorable or would require repeated, invasive treatment to maintain

There’s extensive infection, bone loss, or pain that affects quality of life

The patient is looking for a stable, long-term alternative to dentures

Function, comfort, and aesthetics can be better achieved with implants than with rebuilding compromised teeth

There is a desire for a fresh start—with proper planning and maintenance going forward

That said, we’re not quick to pull healthy or savable teeth just for the sake of convenience or speed. We avoid full-mouth implants when:

There are healthy teeth that can be predictably maintained

The underlying issue can be corrected with more conservative or staged care

The patient is not ready medically, emotionally, or financially to commit to the demands of implant therapy

Expectations or goals don’t align with what full-arch implants can actually deliver

When We Recommend Rebuilding Your Natural Teeth

If your teeth are still structurally sound—or can be restored predictably—we often recommend rebuilding. That may mean a combination of crowns, bridges, bite therapy, and gum care to stabilize and strengthen what’s already there.

We choose this path when:

Your teeth have a solid foundation, even if they’re worn or broken

There’s not extensive bone loss or active infection

You’re willing to invest in maintenance and follow-through care

You value keeping what’s natural when possible

The benefit? You preserve your own biology, avoid unnecessary surgery, and still regain full function and aesthetics with thoughtful planning. For many people, this is the most conservative and long-term stable approach.

When We Recommend Replacing with Full-Mouth Implants:

In some cases, the foundation simply isn’t stable enough to build on. If the teeth are too compromised, or repeated dental work would only offer short-term relief, full-mouth implants can offer a clean slate—with comfort, stability, and peace of mind.

We recommend this when:

Most or all of your teeth are non-restorable or failing

There’s significant pain, mobility, or infection

Dentures are uncomfortable or limiting, and you want something more permanent

You’re medically and emotionally ready to commit to surgical care and long-term maintenance

The benefit? Predictability. With proper planning, implants can restore your bite, chewing power, and confidence—often with fewer compromises than trying to salvage what’s already failing.

How We Decide Together:

This is never a rushed decision. We look at your full picture—clinically, medically, financially, and personally. Then we walk you through the risks, benefits, and maintenance of each path.

Our only agenda is helping you choose the option that sets you up for long-term health, stability, and peace of mind.

Should we highlight your focus on preserving natural teeth?

Yes

We Don’t Just Restore Smiles—We Protect What Matters.

At Livewell, we believe there’s real value in preserving what nature gave you. That’s why our first instinct is not to pull teeth—it’s to understand them.

Whenever possible, we aim to save and restore your natural teeth. Why? Because your teeth are connected to your bone, your bite, your airway, and your overall health in a way that even the best implants can’t fully replicate.

We’ll always walk you through all your options—including implants when they’re appropriate. But we’ll also be honest about when conservative care can achieve the same goals with less risk and intervention.

This approach takes more time. It requires careful planning, deep diagnosis, and a real relationship. But the results? More trust. More predictability. More dignity in your care.

Because we’re not just here to rebuild—we’re here to protect what you already have, whenever we can.

Would you like to add a quote or belief statement that reflects your philosophy?

Craftsmanship You Can See—and Feel.

Your dental work shouldn’t look like dental work. It should look like you.

That’s why we work with a small, trusted group of master dental technicians—people who treat each restoration like it’s their own. We don’t send cases to high-volume, overseas labs. We collaborate with partners who value precision, aesthetics, and personalization just as much as we do.

One unique part of our process is how we handle shade matching. Instead of relying on a technician’s guess or a basic color tab, we use advanced photo calibration technology that allows us to send ultra-precise color information to our lab. It captures the subtle tones, translucency, and character of your natural teeth—so the final result blends in seamlessly.

This means:

No chalky, one-color crowns

No dark lines or mismatched teeth

Just natural, beautiful results that feel like you’ve always had them

It’s a level of detail most patients have never experienced—but once you do, you’ll understand the difference.

Because to us, this isn’t just dental work—it’s personal. And you deserve to love the way it looks and the way it lasts.

We also discussed medically necessary vs aesthetic aspects of full mouth reconstruction. If there is anything you’d like to add regarding that, feel free to do so.

Full-Mouth Reconstruction Isn’t About Vanity—It’s About Vitality.

People often assume full-mouth reconstruction is purely cosmetic. In reality, it’s not about chasing perfection—it’s about rebuilding what’s been lost so you can eat, speak, and live more comfortably.

We begin with function:

Stabilizing your bite. Restoring your ability to chew confidently. Treating pain or infection. Addressing long-term wear or damage that’s been holding you back—sometimes for years.

Aesthetic improvement is simply a natural byproduct.

If we’re already restoring your smile, we believe it should look as good as it feels. But that doesn’t mean we’re here to give you a Hollywood grin—unless that’s what you want. For many patients, our goal is simply to recreate what you had before: familiar, natural, and totally you.

So whether your priority is comfort, health, or confidence—we’ll meet you there. You get to choose what your smile looks like. We’re here to make sure it works beautifully, lasts long, and reflects the life you want to live.

What procedures do you typically include in your reconstructions?

When we take on a reconstruction case, we’re not just fixing broken teeth—we’re rebuilding a foundation for long-term health, function, and confidence. Every person is different, and so is every treatment plan. That’s why we never start with “what” we’re doing—we start with why things broke down in the first place.

A typical reconstruction might include a combination of:

Bite therapy — We often begin by stabilizing your bite. If the foundation isn’t right, even the best dental work won’t hold up over time.

Crowns, veneers, or onlays — These are used to rebuild worn, cracked, or weakened teeth with strong, natural-looking materials.

Implants or bridges — To replace missing teeth and restore proper function.

Gum therapy — If there’s inflammation or bone loss, we address that first. Healthy gums are non-negotiable for lasting results.

Orthodontics or clear aligners — Sometimes we need to create space or improve alignment before we build.

Digital planning and test-drive smiles — You’ll know what’s coming every step of the way. No surprises.

Night guards — To protect your teeth and investment, especially if clenching or grinding has played a role in the breakdown.

Some patients need just a few thoughtful restorations. Others need full-arch treatment. What matters most is that we treat the cause—not just the symptoms.

We design care that’s personalized, phased, and realistic. Our goal is to help you move from reactive to proactive care—so you’re not just back to baseline, but set up for the long run.

Full-Mouth Reconstruction vs. Cosmetic Dentistry

Understanding the Difference—So You Can Choose What’s Right for You

Full-Mouth Reconstruction

This is health-driven dentistry. It’s for people who are dealing with:

Ongoing dental problems like broken teeth, pain, or bite issues

Difficulty chewing or speaking comfortably

Teeth that are worn down, shifting, or have been patched over and over

A desire to rebuild function and restore quality of life

We start with structure: correcting the foundation, stabilizing your bite, and restoring long-term health. The cosmetic benefit? That comes along because we’re rebuilding everything carefully and intentionally. It’s a bonus—not the goal. And we tailor the final look to you—whether that means keeping it natural or enhancing it more dramatically.

This is for patients who are generally healthy, but want to enhance how their smile looks. It’s about:

Whitening or reshaping teeth

Closing small gaps

Improving symmetry

Elective changes based on your vision

There’s usually no pain, dysfunction, or medical need—it’s about making a good smile even better. We still plan thoughtfully, of course, but the focus is on aesthetics more than rebuilding.

Which One Is Right for You?

If you’re struggling with broken teeth, pain, or a bite that just doesn’t feel right, you may need more than just a cosmetic fix. Full-mouth reconstruction is a more involved process—but it’s one that can change your daily comfort, your health, and your confidence long-term.

Whatever you need, we’re here to help you understand your options, respect your goals, and design care that fits your life—not just your teeth.

# All-on-X Dental Implants in Fairfax Station, VA


A full arch of permanent teeth in as few as four implants.

Planned, placed, and restored by Dr. Chris, start to finish.

Precision-guided surgery for faster healing and lasting results.


## You're Not Looking for Another Temporary Fix


Maybe it started with one tooth. Then a few more. Maybe you've been through rounds of crowns, bridges, or dentures that didn't hold up.

Maybe you've been told your teeth need to come out and you've been sitting on that news, not sure what to do next.

All-on-X replaces a full arch. Four to six implants, placed in one procedure, supporting a complete set of fixed teeth. Not removable. Not temporary.

It works where other options haven't. The angled implant placement uses available bone that traditional implants can't reach. Even patients told they "don't have enough bone" are often candidates.

You'll leave with teeth the same day. In most cases, provisional teeth are placed during surgery. No gap. No waiting months without a smile.

If patchwork fixes aren't cutting it anymore, this page covers how it works, who it's for, and what to expect.


## What Are All-on-X Dental Implants?


An All-on-X implant works differently from a single implant. Instead of one post per tooth, four to six posts are placed at strategic angles across the arch. This helps distribute biting force across the arch and can improve contact with available bone.

What Makes Up an All-on-X Implant:

Post: the titanium root placed in the jawbone

Abutment: the connector between the post and the prosthetic arch

Prosthetic arch: a full set of fixed teeth, custom-designed to match your face and bite


## Are You a Candidate for All-on-X?


You may be a candidate if you have:

Several missing or failing teeth:

‍All-on-X may be a good option when many teeth in one arch can no longer be restored predictably.

Loose or uncomfortable dentures:

‍If removable dentures shift, rub, or limit what you can eat, implant-supported teeth may offer more stability.

Advanced gum disease or bone loss:

‍Some patients with periodontal damage may benefit from a full-arch plan instead of continuing to repair individual teeth.

A desire for a stronger long-term solution:

‍All-on-X is designed for patients who want a more fixed, secure, and functional way to rebuild their smile.


## Why Choose All-on-X at Livewell?


All-on-X is not just implant placement. It is smile design, bite planning, surgery, and final teeth working together from the start.

Why patients choose Livewell:

Implants are planned around the final bridge

Your bite and facial support are considered early

Digital imaging helps guide safer planning

Temporary teeth are planned before surgery when possible

You get a clear roadmap before treatment begins


## All-on-X, Done the Livewell Way


It's not just about placing implants. It's a process designed for lasting function, comfort, and confidence.

Discovery and Diagnosis

CBCT 3D scans map your bone density, nerve pathways, and sinus position. Intraoral scans capture your current bite. Dr. Chris reviews everything with you, including what needs to happen, why it is recommended, and what alternatives may be available.

Custom Treatment Plan

Implant positions are digitally planned for your specific jaw anatomy. Angle, depth, and bone engagement are mapped before surgery day. Your provisional teeth are fabricated in advance so they're ready when you are.

Guided Surgery + Same-Day Teeth

Failing teeth are removed. Implants are placed using computer-guided surgical protocols. In most cases, you leave the same day with a full set of provisional teeth.

You walk in without a functioning smile. You walk out with one.

Healing and Refinement

Over 3-6 months, your implants fuse with bone (osseointegration). Your provisionals function during this time. You eat with them, smile with them. If anything needs adjusting (shape, shade, bite) this is when we fine-tune it.

Final Restoration

Your permanent prosthetic is milled from solid zirconia. Digitally designed, precision-fitted, permanently secured. With proper care and maintenance, zirconia restorations are designed to serve patients for many years.


## One Clear Plan From Surgery to Final Smile


With All-on-X, the details matter. Implant position, bite, gum shape, facial support, and the final teeth all need to work together. When those steps are planned separately, small disconnects can affect comfort, function, and the final look of your smile.

At Livewell Dental, Dr. Chris guides the full process with the end result in mind. That means your surgical plan is connected to your temporary teeth, final restoration, and long-term maintenance from the beginning.

Fewer handoffs between providers

A treatment plan that connects surgery and restoration

Clearer communication at each step

A bite and smile design planned before treatment begins

More continuity from consultation to final teeth

## A Fresh Start. A Smile Built to Last.


A full restoration can feel effortless when it is planned around the whole smile.

There is no one-size-fits-all answer for replacing missing teeth. Dentures, single implants, and All-on-X each solve different problems.

## Implant Experience That Extends Beyond the Practice


Dr. Chris is a Clinical Instructor at Implant Accelerator, where he helps other dentists grow their skills in implant planning and treatment. That teaching role reflects the level of detail he brings to All-on-X cases at Livewell Dental.


## The Right Tools for Better Decisions and Better Comfort


Every tool we use has one job: better information before we start, better precision while we work, and support for smoother healing afterward.


### CBCT 3D Imaging


Before any procedure, we take a cone beam CT scan that shows us your bone in three dimensions. We can see exactly where nerves run, where bone density is highest, and what the safest, most effective implant position looks like for your specific anatomy.


### 3D Printing & Guided Surgery


Using data from your 3D scan, we can design a surgical guide that helps control the planned angle and depth. This supports more precise placement than relying on feel alone.


### CLEAN Implant System


We choose implant systems with strong quality standards and biocompatible surface design. What we place in your body matters, so we do not cut corners on implant selection.


### PRF / PRP / CGF


We may use growth factors derived from a small sample of your own blood to support tissue healing after surgery. This technique can help support the body’s natural healing response around surgical sites.


### Surgical Piezosurgery


An ultrasonic surgical tool that can help us work more precisely around delicate areas. In selected cases, it may reduce trauma to surrounding tissues compared with traditional instruments.


### Modern sedation and comfort techniques


Comfort options help patients feel calmer and more prepared during implant treatment. We review your health history and choose the safest approach for your needs.


## Ready to Stop Patching and Start Over?


All-on-X may give you a clearer long-term path forward. We will evaluate your bone, bite, health, and goals, then explain what is possible in plain terms.

What's the difference between All-on-4 and All-on-X?

All-on-4 uses exactly four implants to support a full arch of teeth. All-on-X means the number of implants is based on your bone, anatomy, bite, and restoration design. Some patients may need four implants, while others may benefit from five or six. The goal is to use the number that gives your restoration a stable foundation, not to force every patient into one formula.

How long does the procedure take?

Surgery day is often about 3 to 5 hours per arch. Many qualifying patients leave the same day with provisional teeth. The full process, from consultation to final restoration, often takes about 4 to 7 months, with most of that time dedicated to healing and integration.

Can I eat normally with All-on-X?

During the healing phase, you will need to follow a soft-food diet to protect the implants as they integrate with the bone. After the final restoration is placed, many patients can return to a much broader diet. Dr. Chris will explain what foods are safe at each stage and how to protect your restoration long term.

How long do All-on-X implants last?

The implants are designed as long-term supports, but their lifespan depends on bone health, gum health, bite forces, hygiene, and maintenance. The prosthetic arch may need repair, maintenance, or replacement over time depending on the material and daily wear. Regular checkups are important for protecting the result.

Does it hurt? What is recovery like?

All-on-X treatment is performed with local anesthesia, and sedation options may be available to help you stay comfortable. You should not feel the procedure itself, though soreness, swelling, and tenderness are normal during healing. Most patients return to light activity within a few days, depending on the complexity of their case and their overall health.

Can I get All-on-X if I have gum disease?

Active gum disease must be addressed before implant placement because infection around the gums and bone can increase the risk of implant complications. If gum disease is present, we treat it first or build gum treatment into the overall plan. In some cases, patients with significant periodontal disease may be better served by a full-arch solution than by continuing to repair individual teeth.

Am I too old for All-on-X?

Age is not a disqualifying factor. What matters is overall health, bone quality, and whether you are healthy enough for the surgical procedure. Many of our All-on-X patients are in their 60s, 70s, and 80s. A thorough evaluation looks at medications, medical history, and healing capacity to make sure the approach is appropriate for you specifically.

How much does All-on-X cost without insurance?

All-on-X replaces a full arch of teeth with a fixed, implant-supported denture, and pricing typically runs $30,000 to $35,000 per arch. The price shifts based on how many implants are placed, the type of prosthesis you choose, and whether your case needs prep work like bone grafts or extractions beforehand.

Good to know: while many insurance plans treat this as a major or cosmetic procedure, some will cover a fixed amount toward the extractions or bridge portion, which can help offset part of the cost.

acceptedAnswer.text: Surgery day is often about 3 to 5 hours per arch. Many qualifying patients leave the same day with provisional teeth. The full process, from consultation to final restoration, often takes about 4 to 7 months, with most of that time dedicated to healing and integration.

mainEntity.name: How long does the procedure take?

acceptedAnswer.text: During the healing phase, you will need to follow a soft-food diet to protect the implants as they integrate with the bone. After the final restoration is placed, many patients can return to a much broader diet. Dr. Chris will explain what foods are safe at each stage and how to protect your restoration long term.

mainEntity.name: Can I eat normally with All-on-X?

acceptedAnswer.text: The implants are designed as long-term supports, but their lifespan depends on bone health, gum health, bite forces, hygiene, and maintenance. The prosthetic arch may need repair, maintenance, or replacement over time depending on the material and daily wear. Regular checkups are important for protecting the result.

mainEntity.name: How long do All-on-X implants last?

acceptedAnswer.text: All-on-X treatment is performed with local anesthesia, and sedation options may be available to help you stay comfortable. You should not feel the procedure itself, though soreness, swelling, and tenderness are normal during healing. Most patients return to light activity within a few days, depending on the complexity of their case and their overall health.

mainEntity.name: Does it hurt? What is recovery like?

acceptedAnswer.text: Active gum disease must be addressed before implant placement because infection around the gums and bone can increase the risk of implant complications. If gum disease is present, we treat it first or build gum treatment into the overall plan. In some cases, patients with significant periodontal disease may be better served by a full-arch solution than by continuing to repair individual teeth.

mainEntity.name: Can I get All-on-X if I have gum disease?

acceptedAnswer.text: Age is not a disqualifying factor. What matters is overall health, bone quality, and whether you are healthy enough for the surgical procedure. Many of our All-on-X patients are in their 60s, 70s, and 80s. A thorough evaluation looks at medications, medical history, and healing capacity to make sure the approach is appropriate for you specifically.

mainEntity.name: Am I too old for All-on-X?

acceptedAnswer.text: All-on-X replaces a full arch of teeth with a fixed, implant-supported denture, and pricing typically runs $30,000 to $35,000 per arch. The price shifts based on how many implants are placed, the type of prosthesis you choose, and whether your case needs prep work like bone grafts or extractions beforehand. Good to know: while many insurance plans treat this as a major or cosmetic procedure, some will cover a fixed amount toward the extractions or bridge portion, which can help offset part of the cost.

# Single Dental Implants in Fairfax Station, VA


Treatment options for one missing or failing tooth

Planned and placed in-house by Dr. Chris when appropriate

3D imaging and guided planning for precise, comfortable care


## A Serious Choice If a Problem Has Been Ignored Long Enough


We work with people who've been compensating. You chew on the other side. You hide the gap when you smile. You've been told a bridge is your only option, but grinding down two healthy teeth to replace one doesn't sit right.

If that sounds familiar, you're in the right place.

You won't chew on that side:

‍One tooth is gone and you've adapted. Your bite has shifted. You're protecting the gap without thinking about it.

You're tired of hiding it:

‍It shows when you smile. When you talk. When you laugh. You've gotten good at covering it, but you're done managing it.

A bridge just isn't what you want:

‍You've been offered one. Maybe you've had one before. But the idea of altering two healthy teeth to replace one doesn't make sense to you.

Schedule Your Consultation

Crown

Abutment

Screw


## What is a Dental Implant?


A single dental implant replaces one missing tooth without using the neighboring teeth for support. The implant post is placed in the jawbone, where it acts like an artificial tooth root. After healing, a custom abutment and crown are attached to restore the visible tooth.

Unlike a traditional bridge, a single implant stands on its own. It does not require reshaping the healthy teeth on either side of the gap. It also helps support the bone in the area where the tooth was lost.

At Livewell Dental, Dr. Chris uses 3D imaging, digital planning, and a custom crown design to help the implant fit your bite, your smile, and your long-term oral health.

Watch Now


### Advanced Implant Training. One Doctor Guiding Your Care.



### Dr. Chris


Dr. Chris doesn't just place implants. He teaches other dentists how to plan and execute complex cases as a Clinical Instructor at Implant Accelerator—one of the most respected advanced training programs in the country.

Clinical Instructor, Implant Accelerator (2023): Teaches advanced implant surgery and restorative planning to practicing dentists nationwide

Fellow, International Congress of Oral Implantologists (FICOI, 2022): Recognition of advanced training and clinical outcomes in implant dentistry

Graduate, Kois Center (2021): One of the most rigorous evidence-based postdoctoral programs in dentistry

Fellow, Academy of General Dentistry (FAGD, 2019): Earned by fewer than 6% of general dentists in the U.S.

In-house surgical placement and restoration: Your implant is planned, placed, and restored by one dentist. No outside referrals. No handoffs.

MEET DR. CHRIS


## How We Place a Single Tooth Implant


Five steps. No guessing. No surprises.

We start with diagnosis and planning

A CBCT scan shows your bone structure in three dimensions. Intraoral scanning captures the position of nearby teeth, and bite analysis helps us understand how forces may affect the implant once it is restored. We measure, analyze, and plan before treatment begins.

Your implant position is planned before surgery

We map the planned angle, depth, and position of the implant based on your bone density, nearby anatomy, and adjacent teeth. When appropriate, a custom surgical guide is 3D-printed to help transfer that plan from the computer to your mouth.

Implant placement and temporary planning

The implant is placed using local anesthesia, and sedation is available if you prefer. In selected cases, a temporary tooth can be provided during healing. If bone density is low, grafting may be recommended before or during implant placement. PRF may also be used to support your body’s natural healing response.

Healing and integration

Over several months, the implant integrates with the surrounding bone. During this time, you may wear a temporary tooth or another temporary solution depending on your case. We monitor healing and guide you on what you can safely chew while the implant stabilizes.

Once the implant is healed, we design and place your permanent crown.

Once the implant has healed, we design and place the final crown. Digital models help guide the fit, and shade-matching tools help the crown blend with your surrounding teeth. The goal is a restored tooth that looks natural, feels comfortable, and functions well.


## The Livewell Smile Collection


Designed with Purpose. Crafted to Belong.


### Perfect 1


One tooth. Perfectly matched. A single restoration (veneer, crown, or bonding) crafted to vanish into your natural smile with microscopic precision.


### Perfect 1


Four front teeth. One magical transformation. Ideal for fixing wear, discoloration, or imbalance in the most visible zone of your smile.


### Perfect 1


Ten upper teeth, harmonized to perfection. Balanced, bright, and confident — ready for any setting, any angle, any moment.

View Our Gallery


## Single Implant vs Bridge vs Partial Denture


Not every situation calls for an implant. Here's how the options stack up.

Dr. Chris will help you compare which option fits your case. Not every situation calls for an implant. If bone density is low and grafting is not the right choice, a bridge may be better. If you need a temporary solution before implant treatment, a partial denture may help during the transition.

Still Not Sure? Let's Talk Through It


## Advanced Training That Supports Precise Implant Care


Dr. Chris is a Clinical Instructor at Implant Accelerator, where he helps other dentists develop their skills in implant planning and treatment. That same attention to planning, documentation, and precision guides single implant care at Livewell Dental.


## The Technology We Use Is Chosen for Accuracy, Not Show


Every piece of equipment we use has a specific job: better information before we start, better precision while we work, and support for smoother healing afterward.


### CBCT 3D Imaging


A cone beam scan shows your jawbone in three dimensions. We see exactly where nerves run, where bone is thickest, and what the safest, most effective implant position looks like for your specific tooth.


### 3D Printing & Guided Surgery


Using data from your 3D scan, we can design a surgical guide that helps control the planned angle and depth. This supports more precise placement than relying on feel alone.


### CLEAN Implant System


We choose implant systems with strong quality standards and biocompatible surface design. What we place in your body matters, so we do not cut corners on implant selection.


### PRF / PRP / CGF


We may use growth factors derived from a small sample of your own blood to support tissue healing after surgery. This technique can help support the body’s natural healing response around surgical sites.


### Surgical Piezosurgery


An ultrasonic surgical tool that can help us work more precisely around delicate areas. In selected cases, it may reduce trauma to surrounding tissues compared with traditional instruments.


### Modern sedation and comfort techniques


Comfort options help patients feel calmer and more prepared during implant treatment. We review your health history and choose the safest approach for your needs.


## Start With Clarity, Not Commitment


At Livewell, every reconstruction begins with a comprehensive evaluation before any decision is made. You leave that first visit knowing exactly what is going on, what the options are, and what the path forward looks like.

Call Us

How long does a single tooth implant take from start to finish?

Most cases take 3 to 5 months total. The placement appointment itself is usually under an hour. The majority of the timeline is healing time, while the implant fuses with bone. Once integration is confirmed, the final crown is placed in one or two short visits.

Does getting a dental implant hurt?

The procedure itself is done under local anesthesia, so you won't feel pain during placement. Sedation is also available. Afterward, most patients describe mild soreness for a few days, similar to having a tooth pulled. Over-the-counter medication typically handles it. Many patients return to light activity within a day or two, depending on the complexity of the case and their overall health.

How long do single tooth implants last?

The implant post is designed as a long-term replacement root, but its lifespan depends on bone health, gum health, bite forces, hygiene, and maintenance. The crown on top may need replacement over time due to normal wear.

What's the difference between an implant and a bridge?

A bridge requires filing down the two teeth on either side of the gap to support a connected three-unit restoration. An implant stands on its own. It doesn't touch neighboring teeth. It also preserves the jawbone beneath it, which a bridge cannot do. For many patients with healthy teeth on both sides of the gap, an implant may be the more conservative long-term option.

Can I get an implant if I've had bone loss?

In many cases, yes. If the bone has thinned since the tooth was lost, a bone graft can rebuild the area before or during implant placement. The CBCT scan we take at your first visit shows us exactly how much bone is available and whether grafting is needed.

Will my implant look like a real tooth?

That's the point. The crown is custom-made to match the shade, shape, and surface texture of your surrounding teeth. Dr. Chris designs it to fit your bite and smile line. The goal is a result that blends naturally with your smile.

What happens if I don't replace the missing tooth?

After a tooth is lost, the bone in that area can shrink over time. Nearby teeth may also begin to shift toward the open space, and the bite can change. Over time, this may lead to uneven wear, jaw discomfort, or more complex treatment needs. Replacing the tooth earlier often gives you more straightforward options.

How much would a single dental implant cost?

A single implant — covering the implant post, abutment, and crown — typically runs $3,000 to $6,000. Where you land in that range depends on a few things specific to your case.

The type of implant plays a role (titanium vs. zirconia, standard vs. premium components), and so does the complexity of your case — if you need a bone graft or sinus lift beforehand, that adds to the total. Standard pricing includes your consultation, imaging, the implant placement itself, the abutment, and the crown.

# Sedation Dentistry in Fairfax Station, VA


Sleep through your visit with IV sedation or nitrous oxide

Guided by Dr. Akhavan, board-certified anesthesiologist

Comfort built around you, not a one-size protocol


## Meet Dr. Melody Akhavan, Your Sedation Specialist


For many patients, the idea of “going under” can feel intimidating. That’s why having someone like Dr. Melody Akhavan by your side makes all the difference. With more than 20 years of experience in anesthesia for dental and medical procedures, she has a calm, reassuring way of making even the most nervous patients feel safe, heard, and cared for.

Dr. Akhavan earned her medical degree from the State University of New York School of Medicine, completed her internship in Internal Medicine, and went on to a Residency in Anesthesiology at Winthrop University Hospital, where she served as Chief Resident. She is skilled in all forms of anesthesia, from gentle sedation to general anesthesia, and takes the time to tailor each plan to your specific health needs, comfort level, and treatment.

Her care starts well before your procedure, with a thorough preoperative assessment, and continues until you’re fully awake and feeling well afterward. Her goal is simple: to make your experience as smooth and worry-free as possible, so you can focus on your health, not your fears.

In addition to serving as Anesthesiologist and Assistant Chief of Anesthesiology at Kaiser Permanente earlier in her career, Dr. Akhavan is now President and Lead Anesthesiologist at Capital Anesthesia Associates. We are truly honored to have her caring for our patients.

When she’s not in the operating room, Dr. Akhavan enjoys spending time with her husband and three children, traveling, and giving back through non-profit work.

Watch Now


## Your Dental Care Should Be About You.


The heart of Livewell is built around patients. In-house dental lab, genuine hospitality, and a team that truly cares about you. This is what it means to be looked after from start to finish.

Whether you are visiting for a routine cleaning or a full smile transformation, you will feel seen, supported, and cared for every step of the way.


## Because Fear Shouldn't Stand Between You and Your Health


If dental anxiety has kept you from the chair for years, you know it affects more than your smile. It affects how you feel when you look in the mirror, whether you avoid certain foods, and the quiet worry that sits in the back of your mind when something does not feel right. That is why we have built an experience designed for comfort from the moment you walk in.

It affects more than your next appointment. Dental anxiety left untreated keeps people away for years, and problems that could have been caught early compound into much bigger ones.

Most anxiety goes unaddressed. Not because solutions don't exist, but because most practices don't invest in building an environment where truly nervous patients feel safe enough to show up.

The right experience changes everything. When you know what to expect, who's beside you, and that you're in control, showing up becomes possible. And that's where better oral health begins.


## The Difference You'll Feel Before We Even Start


Dr. Chris knows dental fear firsthand, he had a painful, phobia-inducing dental experience as a child. That’s why he’s spent years refining techniques to make injections virtually undetectable:

Warming the anesthetic to body temperature

Using special distraction methods

Perfecting gentle delivery so patients often don’t feel a thing

Meet Dr. Chris


## Wake Up With Your Smile



### High Level of Comfort


For some, comfort items and gentle techniques are enough. For others, true peace of mind comes from knowing they can sleep through their treatment and wake up with a healthier smile.


### IV Sedation


IV Sedation – The deepest level of relaxation available in a dental office. Perfect for those with severe anxiety, complex treatment plans, or anyone wanting everything done in one visit.


### Nitrous Oxide


A lighter option that eases tension and wears off quickly—no downtime needed.


## Uncompromising Excellence



## Ready to Experience the Livewell Difference?


We welcome patients who value doing things right the first time, with intention, purpose, and partnership. If you have been looking for something different, this is it.

Experience The Livewell Difference

Hear From Our Patients

Who is a good candidate for sedation dentistry?

Sedation dentistry is a good fit for patients with dental anxiety or phobia, anyone who needs several procedures completed in one visit, patients with a strong gag reflex, or anyone who simply prefers to have no memory of the treatment. Dr. Chris will discuss which option makes the most sense based on your health history and what is planned for your visit.

What types of sedation are available at Livewell Dental?

Three options: IV sedation (deepest level of in-office relaxation, ideal for significant anxiety or complex treatment), nitrous oxide (lighter, wears off quickly, no downtime needed), and comfort-first techniques including warmed anesthetic, distraction methods, and a gentle delivery approach that makes injections virtually undetectable for most patients.

Will I be unconscious with IV sedation?

Most patients have little to no memory of the procedure with IV sedation. You will be in a deeply relaxed state and monitored the entire time by Dr. Melody Akhavan. You will need someone to drive you home and should plan to rest for the rest of the day.

How long does recovery take after IV sedation?

Most patients feel alert within a few hours. You will need a designated driver and should avoid operating machinery for the rest of the day. Nitrous oxide wears off within minutes and typically requires no downtime at all.

mainEntity.name: Who is a good candidate for sedation dentistry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three options: IV sedation (deepest level of in-office relaxation, ideal for significant anxiety or complex treatment), nitrous oxide (lighter, wears off quickly, no downtime needed), and comfort-first techniques including warmed anesthetic, distraction methods, and a gentle delivery approach that makes injections virtually undetectable for most patients.

mainEntity.name: What types of sedation are available at Livewell Dental?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients have little to no memory of the procedure with IV sedation. You will be in a deeply relaxed state and monitored the entire time by Dr. Melody Akhavan. You will need someone to drive you home and should plan to rest for the rest of the day.

mainEntity.name: Will I be unconscious with IV sedation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients feel alert within a few hours. You will need a designated driver and should avoid operating machinery for the rest of the day. Nitrous oxide wears off within minutes and typically requires no downtime at all.

# Smile Makeovers in Fairfax Station, VA


Natural results designed around your face

Preview your smile before you commit

Planned by Dr. Chris and crafted with experienced ceramists


## Because Sometimes, “Good Enough” Isn’t Enough


A small touch-up may not be enough when what you really want is a turning point. Whether it is a wedding, a career-defining presentation, a milestone birthday, a reunion, or simply the everyday confidence of liking what you see in the mirror, a smile makeover is designed around the moment that matters to you.

A smile makeover isn't a single procedure. It's a complete reimagining of your smile, covering color, shape, bite, and harmony, crafted to look naturally like you, only better.

At Livewell Dental, we combine the art of cosmetic design with the science of restoring function. Whether you've lived with worn, mismatched, missing, or damaged teeth for years, or you've simply never truly loved your smile, we bring every tool, every skill, and every detail to the table.

Start Your Makeover Journey


## When Everything Falls Into Place


Imagine walking into that moment knowing your smile is the last thing you are worried about.


### The Wedding Day


You have planned every detail, and your smile will be part of the photos you keep for life. With one patient at a time care, careful planning, and natural-looking design, we help you feel confident from every angle without looking overdone.


### A Second Chance at Love


A new chapter deserves a fresh start. Because Dr. Chris is one of the few dentists trained in both advanced cosmetics and complex restorative work, your smile will feel as good as it looks, even if we're rebuilding what you thought was beyond repair.


### Career-Defining Moments


Whether it is a TV appearance, a promotion, or a keynote speech, a confident smile can help you feel more prepared. Digital smile previews let you see the planned result before treatment begins.


### Reunions & Milestones


High school reunions, milestone birthdays, retirement parties, show up feeling like the best version of yourself. Our planning and technology help us work within your timeline without cutting corners.


### Everyday Joy


Sometimes the “big moment” is simply waking up and liking what you see in the mirror. We design smiles that fit your personality, lifestyle, and long-term health.

Let’s Create Your Moment


## A Complete Transformation, Planned to Perfection


Invisalign / Orthodontics

Custom-made shells bonded to the front of your teeth. They change the shape, shade, and proportion of each tooth individually. At Livewell, every veneer is designed using dentofacial analysis and fabricated by master ceramists who specialize in natural-looking restorations.

learn more

When a tooth needs more than surface-level change, a crown restores its full shape and strength while matching the aesthetics of the surrounding teeth. Often part of a makeover when structural and cosmetic needs overlap.

Professional-grade whitening that goes beyond what strips and trays can reach. Used as a standalone treatment or as a finishing step to match veneers, crowns, or bonding to the brightest natural shade your teeth can achieve.

Composite resin applied directly to the tooth to repair chips, close small gaps, or reshape edges. Conservative, often completed in a single visit, and blended to match the exact shade and texture of your natural teeth.

When too much gum tissue makes teeth look short or uneven, recontouring reshapes the gumline to create symmetry and proportion. The frame matters as much as the teeth inside it.

Alignment correction before or alongside cosmetic work. Straightening your teeth first can reduce the amount of reshaping or bonding needed, which means a more conservative final result.


## Leading You Every Step of the Way


Dr. Chris is a graduate of the UCSF School of Dentistry and its AEGD residency program.

He completed advanced training at the Kois Center, one of the most rigorous postgraduate institutions in comprehensive dentistry, and earned Fellowship in both the Academy of General Dentistry and the International Congress of Oral Implantologists.

His training in cosmetics, restorative dentistry, bite function, and complex treatment planning helps him design smile makeovers that look natural and function comfortably.

DDS, UCSF School of Dentistry (2015)

AEGD Residency, UCSF (2016)

Fellow, Academy of General Dentistry (FAGD)

Graduate, Kois Center (2021)

Fellow, International Congress of Oral Implantologists (FICOI)

MEET DR. CHRIS


## Smile Makeovers, Done the Livewell Way


Your makeover follows a blueprint. Every step is designed, reviewed, and confirmed before anything permanent happens. You will know what your result looks like before we begin.

Discovery and Design

We photograph your face, your teeth, and your smile from every angle that matters. Using dentofacial analysis and digital smile design, Dr. Chris maps the relationship between your teeth, your lips, your jawline, and your facial proportions. The goal is a design that belongs to your face, not a template pulled from a catalog.

Preview You Can Try On

Before any tooth is touched, you see your result. A physical preview is built so you can wear your new smile temporarily, check it in different lighting, and decide whether it feels right. If something needs to change, it changes now, not after the final restorations are placed.

Preparation

Once the design is locked, the teeth are prepared. For veneers, this means minimal reshaping of the front surface. For crowns, a more complete reduction. For bonding, often no preparation at all. The approach depends on the tooth and the restoration, not a standard formula.

Handcrafted Fabrication

Your restorations are built by experienced ceramists who receive the full photography package, digital design, and specific shade instructions captured with PolarEyes. The goal is a close partnership where the ceramist understands the same details Dr. Chris sees.

Delivery and Final Verification

Each restoration is tried in, checked against the original design, and verified for shade, fit, and bite before it is permanently bonded. We photograph the final result and compare it to the plan. What you approved is what you get.


## Where Advanced Training Meets Artistry


Beautiful, natural-looking results come from more than technique. Dr. Chris's training at the Kois Center and his close work with a master ceramist mean every veneer and cosmetic restoration is shaped around your face, your bite, and the way you want to feel when you smile.


## The Livewell Smile Makeover Experience


Your makeover is not just a set of procedures. It is an experience designed to feel comfortable, personal, and carefully planned. This is where science, artistry, and one-on-one care come together.


### Surgical Piezosurgery


One-patient-at-a-time visits allow our team to focus fully on your care.


### Ceramist Partnership


We partner with experienced ceramists so restorations are carefully crafted, not treated like factory-made pieces.


### Technology


Digital previews help you understand the planned result before permanent treatment begins.


### Scheduling


Flexible scheduling supports both time-sensitive events and carefully phased treatment plans.


### Expertise


Experience in implants, full-mouth rehabilitation, and aesthetics helps us manage complex smile transformations under one roof.


## The Livewell Smile Collection


Designed with Purpose. Crafted to Belong.


### Perfect 1


One tooth. Perfectly matched. A single restoration (veneer, crown, or bonding) crafted to vanish into your natural smile with microscopic precision.


### Magic 4


Four front teeth. One magical transformation. Ideal for fixing wear, discoloration, or imbalance in the most visible zone of your smile.


### Social 10


Ten upper teeth, harmonized to perfection. Balanced, bright, and confident — ready for any setting, any angle, any moment.

Watch Now

"The most important thing in dentistry happens outside the dental chair."


## Not Rushed. Not Templated. Designed Around You.


Your first visit is not a sales pitch. It is a comprehensive examination with full imaging, clinical photography, and a case presentation where you see everything we see before any recommendation is made. That is the standard for every patient, whether the plan involves one tooth or ten.

One patient at a time. No double-booking, no rotating providers.

Every case documented with photography at every stage, from diagnosis to final result.

Your result previewed and approved before anything permanent begins.

Comfort built into every visit: noise-cancelling headphones, warm blankets, aromatherapy.

Schedule a Consultation

What is a smile makeover and what does it include?

A smile makeover is a combination of cosmetic dental procedures planned and executed together to transform the appearance of your smile. It can include porcelain veneers, dental crowns, teeth whitening, bonding, gum recontouring, and orthodontic alignment. The specific combination depends on your goals, your facial structure, and the current condition of your teeth. At Livewell, every makeover is designed using photography, digital mapping, and a physical preview before anything permanent begins.

Can I see what my smile will look like before I commit?

Yes. Before any permanent work begins, a physical preview is created so you can wear your new smile temporarily and evaluate it in real life. If the shape, shade, or proportion needs adjusting, those changes happen before anything is finalized. You approve the result before it becomes permanent.

How long does a smile makeover take from start to finish?

The timeline depends on the scope. A bonding-only case may take one or two visits. A full veneer case typically takes three to six weeks from preparation to final placement. Multi-phase makeovers that include orthodontics or gum work can extend to several months. Dr. Chris gives you a clear timeline at your consultation based on what your plan involves.

Are smile makeovers covered by insurance?

Most dental insurance plans classify smile makeovers as elective cosmetic treatment and do not cover them. However, individual components like crowns may receive partial coverage if they also serve a functional purpose. Our team reviews your benefits before treatment begins and walks you through what, if anything, applies.

What is the difference between Perfect 1, Magic 4, and Social 10?

These describe the scope of the makeover. Perfect 1 focuses on a single tooth, matched perfectly to the surrounding teeth. Magic 4 covers your four front teeth, transforming the center of your smile. Social 10 addresses all ten upper teeth visible when you smile or speak. The right scope depends on your goals and your starting point, which is determined during your consultation.

How do I know if I need a smile makeover or just veneers?

A smile makeover may include veneers, but it can also include whitening, bonding, gum reshaping, alignment, or crowns. The difference is that a makeover is a coordinated plan where every element is designed together for a cohesive result. If only your front teeth need attention and the rest of your smile is in good shape, veneers alone may be enough. If the changes involve multiple areas or procedures, a makeover gives you a single plan rather than piecemeal treatments.
