# Wisdom Teeth Removal in Fairfax Station, VA



## What Is Wisdom Teeth Removal?


Wisdom teeth are the last molars to develop, usually in the late teens or early twenties. For some people, they grow in normally. For many others, there simply is not enough room.

When wisdom teeth are trapped under the gums, angled toward other teeth, or only partly erupted, they can lead to pain, swelling, cavities, gum infection, and pressure in the jaw.

Wisdom teeth removal is a planned procedure that removes these teeth before they create bigger problems. The goal is to protect your comfort, your bite, and the health of the teeth around them.


## When Should Wisdom Teeth Be Checked?


You may benefit from an evaluation if you notice:

Pressure or soreness in the back of the mouth

‍A dull ache near the jaw, gums, or back molars can be a sign that wisdom teeth are pushing or trapped.

Swollen or irritated gums

‍Partially erupted wisdom teeth can be hard to clean, which may lead to inflammation or infection.

Crowding or shifting teeth

‍Wisdom teeth can sometimes place pressure on nearby teeth, especially when space is limited.

Food trapping behind the molars

‍When wisdom teeth are partly visible, the area can collect bacteria and become difficult to keep clean.


## Benefits of Wisdom Teeth Removal



### Prevents Pain and Infection


Removing problem wisdom teeth can help stop recurring swelling, gum irritation, and jaw discomfort.


### Protects Surrounding Teeth


Wisdom teeth can damage nearby molars or create areas that are difficult to clean. Removal helps protect those teeth.


### Reduces Risk of Future Complications


Early evaluation and timely removal can make treatment simpler before pain, infection, or cysts develop.


## The Wisdom Teeth Removal Process


Evaluate. Plan. Remove carefully

Exam & Digital Imaging

We take a close look at your wisdom teeth, their position, root shape, and relationship to nearby structures.

A Clear Recommendation

Dr. Chris explains whether removal is needed now, can be monitored, or should be planned before symptoms get worse.

Comfort Planning

We review what to expect during the visit, how we will keep you comfortable, and how to prepare before your appointment.

Gentle Tooth Removal

The wisdom teeth are removed using a careful approach based on their position, whether they are erupted, partially erupted, or impacted.

Recovery Instructions & Follow-Up

You receive clear home-care steps for swelling, food choices, cleaning, and healing so recovery feels easier to manage.


## Wisdom Teeth Care That Feels Clear, Calm, and Planned


Wisdom teeth removal can feel intimidating, especially if you are already in pain or nervous about surgery. At Livewell Dental, we slow the process down, explain what we see, and help you understand the safest path forward.

We do not recommend removal just because wisdom teeth exist. We look at your symptoms, imaging, age, tooth position, and risk for future problems before creating a plan.

Why patients choose Livewell:

Digital imaging to understand tooth position clearly

Honest guidance about whether removal is needed

Comfort-focused care for anxious patients

Simple recovery instructions before you leave

A team that explains every step without rushing you

MEET DR. CHRIS


## Trusted by Patients Who Want a Better Surgical Experience


Patients choose Livewell Dental because they want to feel informed before making decisions. Wisdom teeth treatment is not just about removing teeth. It is about preventing future pain, protecting nearby molars, and helping you recover with confidence.

From the first scan to the final recovery instructions, our team is here to make the experience feel more manageable, personal, and clear.

Schedule a Consultation

Do all wisdom teeth need to be removed?

No. Some wisdom teeth can stay if they are healthy, fully erupted, easy to clean, and not causing problems. We recommend removal when they are painful, impacted, infected, or likely to harm nearby teeth.

What does impacted wisdom tooth mean?

An impacted wisdom tooth is trapped under the gums or bone, or angled in a way that prevents it from coming in properly.

When is the best age to remove wisdom teeth?

Many people are evaluated in their teens or early twenties because the roots may be easier to manage before they fully develop. Adults can still have wisdom teeth removed when needed.

Does wisdom teeth removal hurt?

The area is numbed during treatment, and we focus on keeping you comfortable. Soreness, swelling, and jaw stiffness are common afterward, but they usually improve as healing progresses.

How long does recovery take?

Most patients feel significantly better within a few days, though full healing takes longer. We will give you instructions for food, cleaning, swelling, and activity.

# Tooth Extraction in Fairfax Station, VA



## What Is a Tooth Extraction?


A tooth extraction is the removal of a tooth that is damaged, infected, loose, impacted, or no longer able to support your oral health.

While saving natural teeth is always the first goal, there are times when keeping a tooth can lead to more pain, infection, or damage to the surrounding teeth and bone.

At Livewell Dental, we take time to explain why an extraction may be recommended, how the procedure works, and what your options are after the tooth is removed.


## When Might a Tooth Need to Come Out?


You may need an extraction if you have:

A tooth that cannot be restored

‍Severe decay, cracks, or fracture lines can make a tooth too weak to repair predictably.

A painful infection or abscess

‍If infection has spread or the tooth cannot be saved with other treatment, removal may be the safest option.

Advanced gum disease

‍Bone loss around a tooth can make it loose, uncomfortable, or unable to function properly.

A tooth causing crowding or damage

‍Some teeth need to be removed because they are impacting nearby teeth or interfering with a larger treatment plan.


## Benefits of Tooth Extraction



### Relieves Pain and Infection


Removing a problem tooth can help stop ongoing discomfort, swelling, and infection from getting worse.


### Protects Long-Term Oral Health


An unhealthy tooth can affect nearby teeth, gums, and bone. Extraction can help prevent the problem from spreading.


### Prepares for Future Restoration


Once the damaged tooth is removed, we can plan the next step, such as an implant, bridge, or other replacement option.


## The Tooth Extraction Process


Exam & Digital Imaging

We evaluate the tooth, roots, surrounding bone, and nearby structures to understand the safest approach.

Clear Treatment Recommendation

Dr. Chris explains what is happening, why extraction may be needed, and whether any other options are available.

Comfort Planning

Before treatment begins, we review how we will keep you comfortable and what to expect during the visit.

Gentle Tooth Removal

The tooth is carefully removed using a technique based on its condition, root shape, and position in the mouth.

Healing & Next Steps

You receive clear instructions for recovery, and we discuss replacement or preservation options when needed.


## Tooth Removal With Care for What Comes After


At Livewell Dental, extraction is not treated as the end of the story. We focus on your comfort today and your oral health tomorrow.

Before removing a tooth, we consider your symptoms, the condition of the tooth, the health of the surrounding bone and gums, and how the space should be managed after healing.

Clear explanations before any treatment begins

Gentle, comfort-focused care

Digital imaging for safer planning

Honest guidance about saving or removing a tooth

Thoughtful planning for replacement when needed

Start Your Plan


## Trusted by Patients Who Want a Calm, Clear Experience


Patients choose Livewell Dental because they want to feel informed, not rushed. Tooth extraction can feel stressful, especially when you are in pain, so we make the process easier to understand from the first conversation.

Our team will help you know what to expect, how to heal, and what options are available to restore your smile afterward.

schedule a consultation

How do I know if my tooth needs to be removed?

You may need an extraction if the tooth is severely damaged, infected, loose, or cannot be restored in a predictable way. We will examine the tooth and explain your options first. If the tooth can still be saved, treatment such as a root canal may be discussed before extraction.

Does a tooth extraction hurt?

The area is numbed before treatment, and we focus on keeping you comfortable throughout the visit. You may feel pressure, but you should not feel sharp pain during the procedure.

How long does it take to recover?

Most patients begin feeling better within a few days. Full healing takes longer, depending on the tooth, the extraction site, and your overall health.

What should I eat after an extraction?

Soft foods are best at first. Yogurt, eggs, mashed potatoes, smoothies without a straw, applesauce, and lukewarm soup are common options during early healing.

Will I need to replace the tooth after extraction?

It depends on the tooth and your bite. Many extracted teeth should be replaced to protect chewing function, spacing, and bone health. We will explain your options clearly, including dental implants and dental bridges when appropriate.

Can I get an implant after a tooth extraction?

In many cases, yes. Sometimes an implant can be planned soon after extraction. In other cases, the area may need healing or bone grafting first. You can learn more about replacement options on our dental implants page.

Can a tooth be saved instead of removed?

Yes, sometimes. If the tooth still has enough healthy structure and the infection or damage can be treated predictably, Dr. Chris may recommend saving it. Depending on the situation, options may include a root canal, dental crown, or another restorative treatment.

Is tooth extraction the same as wisdom teeth removal?

Not exactly. A tooth extraction can involve any tooth that is damaged, infected, loose, or causing problems. Wisdom teeth removal is a specific type of extraction for third molars, often when they are impacted, painful, or crowding nearby teeth. Learn more about wisdom teeth removal

How much does a tooth extraction cost?

A tooth extraction typically runs $300 to $450. Simple extractions for a visible tooth generally cost less, while impacted or more complex extractions run toward the higher end.

Planned by Dr. Chris with your long-term health in mind


## Most Dentists Tell You What’s Broken. We Tell You Why It Keeps Happening.


A cracked tooth, a failing filling, worn edges, or sensitivity may seem like a single-tooth problem. But often, the real issue is bigger than one damaged area. Your bite, old dental work, clenching habits, tooth structure, and gum health can all affect how long a restoration lasts.

At Livewell Dental, restorative dentistry starts with understanding the cause. Dr. Chris does not just patch what is broken and send you on your way. He evaluates how your teeth work together, why the damage happened, and what type of restoration gives you the best chance at long-term comfort and function.

We look at the cause, not just the damaged tooth

We choose the most conservative option that can protect the tooth

We design restorations to fit your bite, smile, and long-term health

Start With a Full Evaluation


## Find the Right Solution for Your Situation



### Dental Crowns


A dental crown covers and reinforces a tooth that is cracked, weakened, worn down, or heavily restored. Crowns are often recommended when a filling is no longer enough to protect the remaining tooth structure.

Learn About Dental Crowns


### Tooth-Colored Fillings


Tooth-colored fillings repair cavities and small areas of damage using a material designed to blend with your natural tooth. They are a conservative option when enough healthy tooth structure remains.

Learn About Fillings


### Dental Bonding


Dental bonding uses tooth-colored resin to repair small chips, worn edges, gaps, or uneven areas. It can be a simple way to improve the shape or appearance of a tooth without more involved treatment.

Learn About Dental Bonding


### Inlays and Onlays


Inlays and onlays restore teeth with damage that is too large for a filling but may not require a full crown. They help preserve more natural tooth structure while adding strength where the tooth needs support.

Learn About Inlays and Onlays


## How We Work Through Every Case


Restorative care is not just about fixing teeth. It is about understanding why the tooth broke down, choosing the right level of treatment, and protecting your smile for the future.

We Start With the Full Picture

Before recommending treatment, Dr. Chris evaluates the tooth, the surrounding teeth, your bite, gum health, old dental work, and any signs of clenching or grinding. This helps us understand whether the problem is isolated or part of a larger pattern.

We Tell You What Is Needed and Why

You should not have to guess what is happening in your mouth. We explain what we see, why it matters, and what may happen if the issue is left untreated. You will understand the reason behind the recommendation before moving forward.

We Choose the Most Conservative Option

Not every damaged tooth needs a crown. If a filling, bonding, inlay, or onlay can protect the tooth properly, we will discuss that option. The goal is to preserve healthy tooth structure whenever it is predictable and appropriate.

Treatment Is Done With Precision and Comfort

Your restoration is planned around fit, function, and appearance. We use digital tools, careful shade matching, and bite evaluation to help the restoration feel comfortable and blend naturally with your smile.

We Help Protect the Result Long Term

After treatment, we check your bite, review home care, and discuss anything that could affect the restoration over time. If clenching, grinding, or bite stress contributed to the problem, we may recommend a night guard or follow-up plan to help protect your teeth.


## One Doctor. Your Entire Journey.


estorative dentistry works best when the diagnosis, treatment plan, and final result are connected. At Livewell Dental, Dr. Chris guides your care from the first evaluation through the final restoration.

He looks beyond the damaged tooth to understand your bite, gum health, tooth structure, and long-term goals. That means your treatment is not rushed, pieced together, or treated like a quick repair. It is planned with the same attention to detail whether you need one filling or a more complex restorative plan.

Direct care from Dr. Chris

Private, one-patient-at-a-time appointments

AEGD, UCSF -Digital planning and detailed documentation advanced training beyond dental school

Restorations designed for comfort, function, and a natural look


## The Technology Behind General Dentistry at Livewell


See All Our Technology


### Digital X-Rays


Digital X-rays help us detect cavities, bone changes, failing restorations, and hidden issues that may not be visible during a visual exam.


### CBCT 3D Imaging


When more detail is needed, CBCT imaging gives us a three-dimensional view of your teeth, roots, bone, nerves, and surrounding structures.


### Intraoral Scanner


Digital scanning captures the shape of your teeth and bite without traditional impression trays. These records help us design restorations with better fit and accuracy.


### PolarEyes Shade Matching


PolarEyes helps document tooth shade under controlled lighting so crowns, bonding, inlays, and onlays can be designed to blend more naturally.


### Digital Treatment Planning


Digital records allow Dr. Chris to study your bite, tooth structure, and treatment options before beginning restorative care.


## What Patients Say About Their Results


STORIES OF THE LIVES WE’VE TOUCHED

What is restorative dentistry?

Restorative dentistry focuses on repairing damaged, decayed, worn, or missing tooth structure. It includes treatments like tooth-colored fillings, dental crowns, bonding, inlays, and onlays. The goal is to restore comfort, function, strength, and appearance while preserving as much healthy tooth structure as possible.

How do I know if I need a filling, crown, inlay, or onlay?

The right option depends on how much healthy tooth structure remains, where the damage is located, and how much force the tooth handles when you bite. A small cavity may only need a filling. A larger damaged area may need an inlay or onlay. A cracked, weakened, root canal-treated, or heavily restored tooth may need a crown. Dr. Chris will explain which option fits your case and why.

Will my restoration look natural?

Yes, the goal is for your restoration to blend with your natural teeth. We consider tooth color, shape, contour, bite, and smile line when planning restorative treatment. Depending on the treatment, we may use digital design and shade-matching tools to help create a natural-looking result.

Is restorative dental treatment painful?

Restorative treatment is performed with local anesthesia when needed, so you should not feel pain during the procedure. You may feel pressure, vibration, or mild tenderness afterward depending on the treatment. If you feel anxious, we can also discuss comfort options before your appointment.

How long do dental restorations last?

The lifespan of a restoration depends on the material, size of the restoration, bite forces, oral hygiene, clenching or grinding habits, and regular dental maintenance. Fillings, bonding, crowns, inlays, and onlays can all last for years with proper care, but they may need repair or replacement over time.

Does dental insurance cover restorative dentistry?

Many dental insurance plans provide partial coverage for restorative treatment when it is needed to repair decay, damage, or tooth structure. Coverage depends on your plan, diagnosis, and frequency limits. Our team can help review your benefits and explain your estimated out-of-pocket cost before treatment begins.

# No Prep Veneers In Livewell Dental


Little-to-no enamel removal

Natural smile design

Virtual review first

Start Your Virtual Consultation


## You Want a Better Smile. You Don’t Want to Regret the Process.


Veneers can feel exciting until one question gets in the way:

Will healthy teeth have to be shaved down?

That hesitation is reasonable. Enamel is valuable, and once it is removed, it cannot be put back. At Livewell Dental, we begin with a more careful question: can we create the smile you want while preserving as much natural tooth structure as possible?

A permanent decision

‍Your smile should be improved with care, not rushed into irreversible treatment

A conservative first look

‍We study your tooth shape, enamel, bite, and smile goals before recommending veneers.

A clearer path forward

‍Sometimes no prep is possible. Sometimes another option is better. Either way, you should know why.

The goal is not just a prettier smile. It is a smile you can feel good about choosing.


## Meet Your Guide



### Dr. Chris


Dr. Chris approaches cosmetic dentistry with one priority first: protect what is healthy.

A smile is not just a row of teeth. It is part of your face, your expression, your bite, and the way you move through life. Before recommending veneers, Dr. Chris looks at enamel, tooth position, facial balance, lip support, color, gum shape, and long-term function.

UCSF-trained dentist

‍Advanced clinical foundation with a thoughtful, evidence-based approach.

Kois Center GraduateTraining focused on complete care, function, and long-term stability.

Fellow, Academy of General DentistryA distinction earned through extensive continuing education.


## What Are No Prep Veneers?


Thin Porcelain Layer

Natural Edge Shape

No prep veneers are thin porcelain veneers placed with little to no removal of healthy enamel. For the right patient, they can improve the shape, color, size, and balance of the smile by adding carefully designed porcelain instead of aggressively reducing natural teeth.

A brighter smile without an artificial look.

More even edges, proportions, and symmetry.

A fuller look for small, narrow, or worn teeth.

A broader smile when teeth sit slightly inward.


## Are You the Right Candidate for No Prep Veneers?


No prep veneers work best when your smile has room to accept a small amount of added porcelain. That usually means the teeth can be enhanced without looking thick, heavy, or unnatural.

Teeth that feel small or narrow

‍No prep veneers may add fuller shape and better balance.

A smile that feels slightly set back

‍Porcelain can sometimes bring the smile forward in a natural way.

Worn or uneven edges

‍Careful design can restore length, shape, and symmetry.

Healthy enamel

‍Strong enamel helps create a more predictable bond.

Find Out If No Prep Is Right for You

If no prep is not the right fit, that is not bad news. It simply means your smile may need a different conservative path.


## Virtual consultaion


Begin Online Review

01


### Upload Your Photos


Send a few clear, natural photos from your phone. No filters. No special lighting. Just a real look at your smile.

Full smile photo

Resting face photo

Close-up smile photo

02


### Share your smile goals


Tell us what bothers you and what you hope to change.

Maybe you want a brighter smile.

Maybe your teeth feel small or uneven.

Maybe you have old bonding.

Maybe you like the idea of veneers, but you are nervous about shaving healthy teeth.

03


### Get personal feedback


Once we have your photos and your goals, your part is done.

Now we go to work.

Dr. Chris will review your smile and help you understand whether no prep veneers may be worth exploring — or whether another conservative path may make more sense.

This is not a final diagnosis. It is a thoughtful first step.


## See What’s Possible Before Anything Is Permanent


If you have been thinking about veneers but hesitating because you do not want healthy teeth shaved down, start with a careful first look.

Send your photos. Share what you want to change. Dr. Chris will help you understand whether no prep veneers may be possible, or whether another conservative path makes more sense.

Schedule Your Consultation

Call Us


## eLab Technology: Where Digital Science Meets Dental Art


Because You Deserve Better Than “Close Enough”

Natural-looking veneers depend on details most people never see. Shade, translucency, texture, edge shape, facial balance, and how the teeth reflect light all matter.

At Livewell Dental, digital planning and eLab-style communication help Dr. Chris and the lab design veneers with more precision before anything is finalized. The goal is simple: a smile that looks polished, but still belongs to your face.

Shade with intention

‍We study color so the result does not look flat, opaque, or overly white.

Shape with restraint

‍The design is planned to avoid a bulky or overbuilt look.

Details before delivery

‍Photos, scans, and planning help guide the final ceramic work.

Am I a candidate for no prep veneers?

You may be a good candidate if your teeth are slightly small, narrow, worn, or set back, and there is room to add porcelain naturally. If your teeth are crowded, prominent, very dark, or heavily restored, another option may be more appropriate.

Will no prep veneers look bulky?

They can look bulky if they are forced into the wrong case. That is why planning matters. Dr. Chris evaluates your tooth position, smile shape, enamel, and bite before deciding whether no prep veneers make sense.

Can veneers fix small or narrow teeth?

Yes, in many cases veneers can improve tooth size, shape, and smile width. No prep veneers are often most successful when the smile can be enhanced by adding carefully designed porcelain. For broader cosmetic planning, you may also want to review our smile makeover page.

What if I am not a no prep candidate?

That does not mean you are out of options. Depending on your smile, Dr. Chris may recommend teeth whitening, dental bonding, gum recontouring, alignment, minimal-prep veneers, or a more complete cosmetic plan.

How long do no prep veneers last?

With good planning, strong bonding, proper bite management, and regular dental care, porcelain veneers can last many years. Longevity depends on your enamel, bite, habits, and how well the veneers are maintained.

What photos should I send for a virtual consultation?

Send a full smile photo, a relaxed resting photo, a side or angle photo, and a close-up smile photo. You can also include an inspiration photo if there is a smile style you like. No filters or special lighting are needed.

Can I get veneers if I grind my teeth?

Grinding does not disqualify you from veneers, but it does need to be addressed before and after treatment. Uncontrolled grinding puts veneers at risk of chipping or failing early. At Livewell, every case begins with a bite evaluation. If grinding is a factor, Dr. Chris will discuss how to protect your result long-term before a single veneer is placed.

# Services at Livewell Dental


Treatment at Livewell starts with understanding.

Before recommending anything, Dr. Chris evaluates your teeth, bite, gum health, and long-term goals. What you receive is a plan built around your situation, not a menu of procedures pushed in your direction.


## Before Any Treatment, You Need the Right Picture


Most dental visits start with a list of what is broken. At Livewell, we start with a different question: why did it break, and what does your mouth actually need long-term?

The dCOE is a structured, multi-step evaluation that looks at your health, bite, function, and aesthetics together before any treatment is recommended.

The most thorough exam most patients have ever had

Covers health, function, and aesthetics as one connected system

You leave with a full report and a plan built around your goals

Start With a Full Evaluation


## Cosmetic Dentistry


Cosmetic dentistry at Livewell is not about making teeth look generically perfect. It is about designing a smile that fits your face, your proportions, and the way you actually look when you speak and smile. Every cosmetic plan starts with dentofacial analysis and digital design before any treatment begins.

Most dental problems do not announce themselves. They build quietly over months or years until something breaks down. General dentistry at Livewell is built around catching those problems early, managing risk before it becomes damage, and keeping your mouth healthy enough that more serious treatment stays off the table.

What dental services does Livewell Dental offer in Fairfax Station, VA?

Livewell Dental offers general dentistry, cosmetic dentistry, restorative dentistry, dental implants, oral surgery, and orthodontics. Specific services include professional cleanings, porcelain veneers, dental crowns, bone grafting, sinus lifts, All-on-X implants, Invisalign, and full mouth reconstruction, among others. Every service is planned and delivered by Dr. Chris with the same standard of care regardless of the complexity of the case.

How do I know which dental service I need?

The best starting point is a thorough evaluation, not a guess. At Livewell Dental, the dCOE — Detailed Comprehensive Oral Evaluation is designed for exactly this situation. It looks at your bite, gum health, tooth structure, aesthetics, and function together and produces a clear report and treatment plan based on what is actually happening in your mouth, not just what is visible on a quick exam.

Does Livewell Dental offer dental implants?

Yes. Dr. Chris plans, places, and restores dental implants in-house. Options include single tooth implants, implant-supported bridges, All-on-X full-arch implants, and locator-retained dentures. Every implant case begins with CBCT 3D imaging and digital planning before any procedure is scheduled.

What cosmetic dentistry services are available at Livewell Dental?

Livewell offers porcelain veneers, no-prep veneers, teeth whitening, gum recontouring, and full smile makeovers. Every cosmetic plan starts with dentofacial analysis and digital smile design so the result fits your face and proportions, not a generic template.

Does Livewell Dental offer sedation for anxious patients?

Yes. Sedation dentistry options are available and can be discussed before any appointment. If you feel anxious about a procedure, comfort options are available and are reviewed as part of your treatment planning, not as an afterthought.

Does Livewell Dental accept dental insurance?

Livewell Dental works with many dental insurance plans. Benefits are reviewed before treatment begins and a full cost breakdown is provided in advance. Financing options are also available for cases where out-of-pocket costs are a concern. Learn more about insurance and financing at Livewell.

How long does full mouth reconstruction take?

The timeline for full mouth reconstruction depends on the complexity of the case, the number of teeth involved, and whether preparatory procedures like bone grafting or implant placement are needed. Some cases are completed in a few months. Others with significant structural changes may take longer. Dr. Chris provides a clear timeline and phased plan at your evaluation so you know what to expect before treatment begins.

# Oral Surgery at Livewell Dental


Procedures planned with 3D imaging before anything begins

Piezo surgery and PRF for precise, comfortable healing

Performed by Dr. Chris, start to finish


## Most Surgeries Start With the Tooth. We Start With the Cause.


A tooth that needs to come out usually failed for a reason. Bone that needs rebuilding before an implant can be placed requires understanding what was lost and why. At Livewell Dental, Dr. Chris evaluates the full picture before recommending any procedure, so the surgical plan connects to your long-term goals from the start.

We identify the cause before recommending surgery

Every case planned with CBCT imaging and digital records

Comfort options available for anxious or complex cases

Start With a Full Evaluation


## FIVE PROCEDURES. ONE STANDARD OF CARE.



### Wisdom Teeth Removal


When wisdom teeth are impacted, infected, or crowding adjacent teeth, removal protects the surrounding bone and neighboring molars. Dr. Chris evaluates position, root shape, and risk before recommending extraction.

Learn More


### Tooth Extraction


When a tooth cannot be saved, careful removal protects the bone and prepares the site for what comes next. Every extraction is planned with the long-term restoration already in mind.


### Sinus Lift


When bone height in the upper jaw is too low for implants, a sinus lift elevates the membrane and places graft material to create the space needed.


### Bone Grafting


Bone lost after extraction or gum disease can make implant placement impossible. Grafting rebuilds that structure so the site can support a long-term restoration.


### Ridge Augmentation


After tooth loss, the jaw ridge shrinks in width and height. Augmentation restores the natural contour so implants seat correctly and final restorations look natural.


## How We Approach Every Surgical Case


Planning before the procedure means fewer surprises during recovery.

Imaging and Full Diagnosis

Before anything is recommended, Dr. Chris reviews a CBCT 3D scan, clinical photographs, and intraoral scans. This gives him a complete picture of your bone volume, nerve location, sinus anatomy, and the condition of surrounding teeth. For oral surgery, this level of detail is not optional, it is what allows the plan to be accurate before the first appointment begins.

Cause First, Procedure Second

Teeth do not fail without a reason, and bone does not disappear without cause. Before recommending extraction, grafting, or any surgical procedure, Dr. Chris evaluates what led to the problem and what the site will need after healing. That might be an implant, a bridge, or simply protecting the surrounding structure. The surgical recommendation follows the diagnosis, not the other way around.

Least Invasive Approach That Works

Where possible, Dr. Chris uses piezo surgery, which cuts bone with ultrasonic precision while protecting surrounding nerves and soft tissue. PRF or PRP therapy, derived from your own blood, may be used at the surgical site to support healing. Comfort options are discussed before the appointment so you know exactly what to expect.

Clear Recovery From Day One

Before you leave, you receive specific instructions for food, cleaning, swelling, and activity. Follow-up visits are scheduled to confirm healing is progressing. If an implant or restoration follows the surgery, that next step is coordinated from the beginning so nothing falls through the gap between providers.


## One Doctor. Guides Every Step


When different providers handle different parts of a surgical case, information gets lost between handoffs. The surgeon may not know the restorative plan. The restorative dentist may not have seen the original imaging. Small disconnects at each stage can affect how the site heals, how the implant is positioned, and how the final result looks and functions.

At Livewell Dental, Dr. Chris reads your imaging, plans the procedure, performs the surgery, and monitors your recovery. The surgical plan stays tied to your overall dental health and long-term goals from the first visit forward.

Direct care from Dr. Chris throughout

Private, one-patient-at-a-time appointments

CBCT imaging, piezo surgery, and PRF healing support

Restorations planned for function and long-term stability


## The Technology Behind Oral Surgery at Livewell


Our Technology


### CBCT 3D Imaging


Standard X-rays show a flat image of a complex three-dimensional structure. CBCT imaging maps your bone density, nerve pathways, sinus floor position, and available implant space in full 3D before surgery begins. For procedures like sinus lifts, bone grafting, and guided implant placement, this detail determines whether a procedure is safe, what approach to use, and how to avoid complications. It is the difference between planning a procedure and guessing through one.


### Intraoral Scanner


Traditional rotary instruments cut through everything in their path, including soft tissue and nerves close to the surgical site. Piezo surgery uses ultrasonic vibration to cut bone selectively, leaving nerves, membranes, and soft tissue intact. For procedures involving the sinus membrane during a sinus lift, or bone removal around sensitive root anatomy, this precision reduces trauma and supports cleaner healing.


### PRF / PRP / CGF


After surgery or grafting, the quality of healing determines whether the site is ready for the next step. PRF, PRP, and CGF are concentrates of growth factors prepared from a small sample of your own blood and applied directly to the surgical site. They support the body's natural healing response, which matters especially in grafting cases where new bone needs to integrate before an implant can be placed.


### 3D Printing and Surgical Guides


When implant placement follows extraction or bone grafting, the position of each implant must be planned around the final restoration, the bite, and the available bone. A digitally designed surgical guide transfers that plan from the screen to the mouth, controlling angle, depth, and position during placement. This is what connects the surgical step to the restorative outcome.


### Intraoral Scanning


Digital scans capture the shape of your teeth, bite, and tissue before and after surgery. These records help Dr. Chris communicate precisely with the lab during restoration design, track changes in tissue or bone over time, and avoid the distortion that can come with traditional impressions.

Does oral surgery hurt?

Oral surgery at Livewell is performed with local anesthesia, so you should not feel the procedure itself. Soreness, swelling, and jaw stiffness are normal in the days following surgery and typically improve with rest and the medications recommended afterward. For patients who feel anxious about surgery, comfort options are available, ask us about sedation dentistry before your appointment.

Do I need bone grafting after every tooth extraction?

No. Whether bone grafting is recommended after an extraction depends on where the tooth was located, how much bone is present, and whether a dental implant or other restoration is planned for that site. In some cases, grafting at the time of extraction helps preserve the bone so future implant placement is more predictable. Dr. Chris evaluates each site individually.

How soon after a tooth extraction can I get a dental implant?

In some cases, an implant can be placed the same day as the extraction. In others, the site needs time to heal, especially if bone grafting was required. The timeline depends on the condition of the bone, the reason for extraction, and how the site heals. You will leave your consultation with a clear estimate. Learn more about dental implants at Livewell.

What is a sinus lift and when is it needed?

A sinus lift is a procedure that increases bone height in the upper jaw when the sinus floor sits too close to the ridge to allow safe implant placement. Bone graft material is placed between the jaw and the sinus membrane after the membrane is gently elevated. It is one of the more common preparatory procedures before upper arch implant treatment.

Does dental insurance cover oral surgery?

Many dental insurance plans provide partial coverage for oral surgery when the procedure is clinically necessary. Coverage depends on your specific plan, the diagnosis, and the type of procedure. Our team reviews your benefits before treatment and gives you a full cost breakdown in advance. You can also learn about financing options if out-of-pocket costs are a concern.


### Common Questions About Oral Surgery at Livewell

# Porcelain Veneers in Mantua, VA


Serving Mantua, VA — about 15 minutes from our Fairfax Station office.

Beautiful, custom-crafted veneers designed around your face, not a formula

eLab digital design helps preview and plan your smile before your veneers are made

Treatments planned and placed by Dr. Chris, personally


## What Are Veneers?


Porcelain veneers are ultra-thin shells of dental ceramic bonded to the front surface of your teeth. They change the shape, color, size, and symmetry of your smile without altering the tooth underneath more than necessary.

What makes veneers different from whitening or bonding is permanence and precision. They are custom-fabricated by an elite ceramist, matched to the specific translucency and shade of your natural teeth, and designed to look like they belong there. Not like veneers. Like your teeth, but the version of them you always wanted.

At Livewell, veneers are never an impulse treatment. Every case starts with a full evaluation of your bite, your tooth structure, and your facial proportions to make sure the result holds up functionally as well as aesthetically.


## Because Every Smile Tells a Story


You are not here because your teeth are broken. You are here because your smile does not feel like you.

See Our Smile Makeovers

You are here because you have lived with something small for a long time. A chip you learned to hide. A shade you never loved. Teeth that look fine to everyone else but feel wrong to you every time you see a photo. Maybe your past dental work left you with restorations that never quite matched. Maybe you have been comparing your smile to the one you had ten years ago.

Veneers are not just about aesthetics. They are about feeling comfortable in your own face again. At Livewell, the goal is never a set of teeth that looks like it came from a catalog. It is a smile that fits your features, matches your personality, and still looks like you, just the best version of it.

Your veneers are not rushed or treated like a mass-production case. They are planned with the same attention to detail we bring to complex restorative work, because your smile deserves careful planning.


## Are You the Right Candidate for Veneers?


Veneers are the right fit for people who want a lasting change. Dr. Chris will tell you honestly if you are one of them.

Staining whitening cannot fix, including intrinsic discoloration, old bonding that has yellowed, or restorations that no longer match.

Small chips, worn edges, or uneven tooth shapes that affect the look of your smile.

Slight misalignment, short teeth, or minor spacing where orthodontics feels like more than you want.

Teeth that are healthy enough for veneers and supported by stable gums and a balanced bite.

Find Out If Veneers Are Right for You


## Why Our Veneers Don’t Look Like “Veneers”


01


### Crafted with Experienced Ceramists


Dr. Chris works closely with skilled ceramists so each veneer is shaped, shaded, and textured to blend naturally with your smile.

02


### Designed for longevity


Veneers are planned around your bite and tooth structure so functional issues are not overlooked.

03


### No Template Smile Design


Your veneers are designed around your facial features, tooth shape, smile line, and goals — not a standard catalog look.

Watch Now


## Where the Precision Comes From


Dr. Chris is a graduate of the Kois Center, one of the most respected clinical training programs in comprehensive dentistry, and a Fellow of both the Academy of General Dentistry and the International Congress of Oral Implantologists. He completed his dental degree and residency at UCSF and teaches advanced techniques to other dentists as a clinical instructor. That background helps him plan veneers with attention to bite, facial balance, tooth structure, and long-term function.

Kois Center graduate, trained in evidence-based treatment planning and aesthetic outcomes

Fellow of the Academy of General Dentistry (FAGD) and the International Congress of Oral Implantologists (FICOI)

Clinical instructor at Implant Accelerator, teaching advanced dentistry nationwide

University of California San Francisco, Doctor of Dental Surgery and General Practice Residency

Meet Dr. Chris


## Veneers, Done the Livewell Way


It is more than putting porcelain on teeth. It is a process designed for lasting function and beauty.

Discovery & Design

Your first visit is not about picking a shade from a chart. Dr. Chris evaluates your oral health, bite, tooth structure, and facial proportions. He asks what you want your result to look like and listens carefully. This conversation shapes everything that follows. No two design plans are identical because no two patients are.

Master-Crafted Porcelain

Your case is created with an experienced ceramist using the specifications Dr. Chris builds around your face, bite, and anatomy. Each veneer is crafted to match the texture, translucency, and depth of natural enamel. This is not a generic lab order. It is a detailed collaboration.

Precision Prep

When preparation is needed, Dr. Chris removes only the minimum amount of tooth structure required for the veneer to bond correctly and sit flush with your gumline. When a no-prep approach is appropriate, nothing is removed at all. Either way, the goal is to preserve as much natural tooth as possible.

Functional Harmony

This step helps reduce unnecessary stress on the veneers and supports a longer-lasting result.

Finishing Touches That Belong

The goal is a smile that looks natural enough to feel like it has always belonged to you.


## One Personalized Plan. A Naturally Beautiful Smile.


Veneers can feel completely natural when each one is designed around the whole smile.


### Before And After


Before

After

Front

Close up

Side view

SEE MORE PATIENT CASES


## A Clinical Instructor, Focused on Cosmetic Detail


Dr. Chris teaches advanced techniques to other dentists, the careful planning, documentation, and precision that separate good dentistry from natural-looking results. He brings that same discipline to every veneer case at Livewell Dental, where the shape, the shade, and the way light moves across each tooth are what make a smile look effortlessly real.


## No-Prep or Traditional Veneers?


Not every case is the same. Dr. Chris will recommend the right approach for your teeth, your goals, and your anatomy during your consultation.

No-Prep Veneers

Traditional Veneers

What it involves

Veneers bonded directly to the tooth surface with little to no enamel removal

A controlled amount of enamel is reduced to create space for the veneer to sit flush and bond correctly

Is it reversible?

In most cases, yes. Because minimal or no tooth structure is altered, removal is possible

No. Once enamel is removed it does not grow back, making this a permanent commitment

Who it suits best

Patients with healthy enamel, minor cosmetic concerns, and teeth that are sized appropriately for added porcelain

Patients seeking more significant shape, length, or color changes that require a slightly thinner tooth surface to achieve the right result

Appearance

Natural and seamless when the case is appropriate for this approach

Equally natural. The reduction allows for more versatility in achieving dramatic changes without the veneers appearing bulky

Longevity

Often 10 to 20 years with proper care, depending on bite, habits, and maintenance

Anesthesia needed?

Rarely

Often, for patient comfort during the preparation stage


## eLab Technology: Where Digital Science Meets Dental Art


Because You Deserve Better Than “Close Enough”

The eLab digital design system allows Dr. Chris to plan your smile in full detail before a single veneer is made. Using digital imaging and design software, he builds a precise model of your proposed result and reviews it against your facial anatomy. You see a detailed preview of your outcome before anything is fabricated. No guessing. No hoping it looks right when it arrives.

Review your smile design digitally before any treatment begins

Precise communication between Dr. Chris and the ceramist helps reduce interpretation errors

Restorations arrive accurately fabricated, reducing chairside adjustment time

The final result is guided by the plan you reviewed and approved

Are veneers permanent?

Traditional veneers require a controlled amount of enamel removal, which makes the decision permanent. The veneers themselves typically last 10 to 20 years, at which point they can be replaced. No-prep veneers, where no enamel is removed, can in most cases be reversed. Dr. Chris will recommend the right approach during your consultation and explain exactly what the commitment looks like for your specific case.

Do veneers damage your teeth?

For traditional veneers, a small amount of enamel is removed so the veneer sits flush and bonds correctly. At Livewell, Dr. Chris removes only what is necessary, no more. When a no-prep approach is appropriate, nothing is altered at all. The goal in every case is to preserve as much natural tooth structure as possible while achieving a result that holds up over time.

Will my veneers look fake?

Veneers should not look fake when they are carefully designed, shaded, and shaped around your natural smile. Every veneer is matched to the exact translucency, surface texture, and shade of your natural teeth by an elite ceramist. The result is meant to look like your teeth, improved, not like dental work. Most patients find that no one notices unless they choose to say something.

Can veneers fix crooked teeth without braces?

In cases of mild misalignment, veneers can correct the appearance of slight spacing, unevenness, or short teeth without orthodontic treatment. For more significant alignment issues, straightening first often leads to a more conservative and longer-lasting veneer result. Dr. Chris will tell you during your consultation which path fits your situation.

What is the difference between Perfect 1, Magic 4, and Social 10?

These are the three veneer scopes available at Livewell, each defined by how many teeth are involved. Perfect 1 is a single restoration, whether a veneer, crown, or bonding, crafted to disappear seamlessly into your existing smile. Magic 4 covers your four front teeth, the zone most visible when you speak or smile. Social 10 treats all ten upper teeth, the full frame of your smile from any angle. The right scope depends on your goals and your starting point, which is determined at your consultation.

How long does getting veneers take?

A typical case at Livewell takes three to six weeks from your design appointment to final placement. The first visit covers evaluation and design. A second visit handles preparation while your veneers are being handcrafted. Final placement and refinement complete the process. If your case includes gum work or other preparatory steps, the timeline extends accordingly. You will know the full schedule before anything begins.

Can I get veneers if I grind my teeth?

Grinding does not disqualify you from veneers, but it does need to be addressed before and after treatment. Uncontrolled grinding puts veneers at risk of chipping or failing early. At Livewell, every case begins with a bite evaluation. If grinding is a factor, Dr. Chris will discuss how to protect your result long-term before a single veneer is placed.

What is the estimated cost of getting porcelain veneers?

Porcelain veneers are priced at $2,500 per tooth. Pricing covers your consultation, digital imaging, temporary veneers while your custom set is made, lab fees, and final placement.

A full smile makeover involving multiple veneers will naturally cost more, since the total scales with the number of teeth treated.

# Dental Implants for Mantua, VA


Livewell Dental welcomes Mantua patients to our Fairfax Station office for implant care with Dr. Chris.

Implants placed and restored in-house

Care led by Dr. Chris

3D imaging and digital planning

Dr. Chris’s Vision for Better Implant Care


## Dental Implant Care for Mantua Patients


Missing a tooth or struggling with a loose denture? Livewell Dental offers single implants, implant bridges, All-on-X, and locator-retained dentures for Mantua patients. Dr. Chris plans, places, and restores implants at our Fairfax Station office, with recommendations based on your oral health, bite, and goals.

Start With a Full Evaluation


## Planned Around Your Bite and Final Teeth


Watch Now

At Livewell, Dr. Chris considers the replacement tooth before planning the implant beneath it. He reviews your bite, gum health, bone, and neighboring teeth so the surgical plan supports the final crown or bridge.

Complete evaluation of your oral health, bone structure, and aesthetic goals

Digital treatment planning to visualize your final result before we begin

Surgical guides when appropriate to support planned implant positioning

Follow-up care to monitor your implants, gums, and bite


## Implant Options at Livewell Dental


Your choice depends on how many teeth need replacing, your bone support, and whether you prefer fixed or removable teeth. Dr. Chris will explain suitable options, treatment stages, and costs at your consultation.


### Single Implants


One implant supports a custom crown to replace a missing tooth. Dr. Chris plans its position and the crown together to fit your bite and surrounding teeth. Healing generally takes several months.


### Implant Bridges


An implant bridge replaces several neighboring teeth without using the adjacent natural teeth as supports. Dr. Chris determines the number of implants needed from the size of the gap, bone support, and bite.


### All-on-X


Multiple implants support a fixed set of upper or lower teeth. Dr. Chris assesses whether this approach suits your case and whether temporary teeth can be fitted on the day of surgery.


### Locator-Retained Dentures


A removable denture snaps onto implants for added stability. You take it out for cleaning. Dr. Chris plans the number and position of implants around your jaw and denture needs.


## Compare Your Implant Options


These are general comparisons. Implant numbers, healing time, and grafting needs vary by patient. Same-day teeth are temporary, and final teeth are fitted after healing.

Still Not Sure? Let's Talk Through It


## One Doctor. Your Entire Journey.


Dr. Chris leads implant planning, placement, and restoration at Livewell Dental. Mantua patients can return to the same Fairfax Station practice for treatment and follow-up. If specialist care is appropriate, Dr. Chris will discuss that with you.

In-House Implant Care. Planning, placement, and restoration at Livewell.

Planned Before Day One. Final crown designed before surgery begins.

3D-Guided Planning. Implant placement is planned with digital imaging and guidance when appropriate.

Sedation Available. Comfort options at every stage.

Fully Documented. Photos and scans tracked throughout.


## Technology Used in Your Implant Care


Livewell uses 3D imaging, digital records, and surgical planning tools to assess your anatomy and plan treatment. Dr. Chris selects the tools appropriate for your case.


### CBCT 3D Imaging


CBCT imaging gives Dr. Chris a three-dimensional view of your jawbone, nerves, and sinuses. It helps him assess bone support and plan implant placement.


### 3D Printing & Guided Surgery


Using data from your 3D scan, we can design a surgical guide that helps control the planned angle and depth. This supports more precise placement than relying on feel alone.


### Implant Selection


We choose implant systems with strong quality standards and biocompatible surface design. What we place in your body matters, so we do not cut corners on implant selection.


### PRF and CGF Healing Support


We may use growth factors derived from a small sample of your own blood to support tissue healing after surgery. This technique can help support the body’s natural healing response around surgical sites.


### Surgical Piezosurgery


An ultrasonic surgical tool that can help us work more precisely around delicate areas. In selected cases, it may reduce trauma to surrounding tissues compared with traditional instruments.


### Modern sedation and comfort techniques


Dr. Chris reviews your health history and anxiety concerns before recommending anesthesia and any suitable sedation options for your implant visit.


## The Craft Behind the Smile


"The most important thing in dentistry happens outside the dental chair."


## Is This the Right Option for You?


An examination is needed to confirm whether implants suit you. Dr. Chris reviews your gums, bone support, medical history, and smoking habits before recommending treatment. These concerns are good reasons to book an assessment.

Check If You Are a Candidate

You have one or more teeth missing

You’ve had a bridge, partial, or denture that never felt quite right

You avoid certain foods or chew on one side

You’ve had repeated dental work in the same area and want something that lasts

You want to compare implant treatment with other replacement options

You want to restore your bite in a way that feels strong, cleanable, and natural


## What Our Patients Are Saying


See All Testimonials


## Clinical Instructor at Implant Accelerator.


Dr. Chris teaches implant dentistry through Implant Accelerator. His training includes UCSF and the Kois Center, and he holds fellowship status with the International Congress of Oral Implantologists. At Livewell, he applies that background to planning your implant and final restoration.


## Why Mantua Patients Choose Implants at Livewell


For Mantua residents, choosing Livewell means implant care led by Dr. Chris at one Fairfax Station practice.

01


### Care Led by Dr. Chris


Dr. Chris plans, places, and restores implants at Livewell, connecting your surgical care with the design of your final teeth.

02


### Planning You Can Understand


Dr. Chris uses your examination and 3D imaging to explain your options, bone support, and the steps involved before treatment begins.

03


### Follow-Up at the Same Practice


Return to our Fairfax Station office for healing checks and ongoing implant care, with a team familiar with your treatment.


## Implants, Done the Livewell Way


Plan for several visits from Mantua for assessment, treatment, and healing checks. Dr. Chris will explain your expected timeline before you begin.

Discovery & Diagnosis

Dr. Chris reviews your dental and medical history, takes a 3D CBCT scan, and evaluates your bone, bite, and gum health to see exactly what your case needs.

Digital Planning & Surgical Guide

Using your scan, Dr. Chris designs the exact implant position and, when helpful, creates a surgical guide that keeps placement precise and predictable.

Implant Placement

Dr. Chris places the implant with local anesthesia and suitable sedation options when needed. You receive instructions for eating, cleaning, and recovery before returning home.

Healing & Provisional

Healing takes place over the following months, with follow-up visits to check progress. Dr. Chris will discuss suitable temporary tooth options for this stage.

Final Restoration

Once healing is complete, your custom, natural-looking crown or bridge is fitted and adjusted until your bite feels right and looks like it belongs there.


## A Livewell Patient’s Before and After


This patient came to Livewell with several missing teeth and failing restorations. A coordinated restorative plan brought their care together and restored a full arch of teeth. These photos show the result featured on Livewell’s implant page.

Before treatment

After treatment

An existing Livewell Dental patient case. Individual results vary. Your treatment options will depend on an examination of your teeth, gums, and bone.

Where do Mantua patients go for implant treatment?

Visit Livewell Dental at 9027 Silverbrook Road, Suite F, Fairfax Station, VA 22039. Our office serves Mantua patients but is located in Fairfax Station. Call (703) 690-0102 to arrange an implant consultation. Allow travel time based on your starting point and traffic.

Can I really get new teeth in one day?

Some patients can receive temporary teeth the same day as implant surgery, especially in certain full-arch cases. It depends on bone quality, overall health, the number of implants, and whether extractions or grafting are needed. Dr. Chris will evaluate your case with 3D imaging and explain whether same-day temporary teeth are appropriate for you.

How long do dental implants last?

With healthy gums, good home care, and regular dental visits, dental implants can last many years. The implant post itself is designed as a long-term replacement root, while the crown, bridge, or prosthesis attached to it may need maintenance, repair, or replacement over time depending on bite forces, materials, and daily habits.

Is dental implant treatment painful?

Dr. Chris uses local anesthesia to numb the treatment area and discusses suitable sedation options when needed. Soreness and swelling can occur afterward. Before you leave Livewell, the team explains recovery instructions and when to contact the office. If sedation is planned, ask about escort and driving requirements before your visit.

What if I do not have enough bone for implants?

If there is not enough bone to support an implant safely, Dr. Chris may recommend bone grafting, sinus lift treatment, ridge augmentation, or a different implant approach. A CBCT scan helps us evaluate bone volume and determine what is possible before treatment begins.

How do I care for dental implants?

Dental implants require daily brushing, careful cleaning around the implant, and regular professional maintenance. Depending on your restoration, we may recommend floss threaders, interdental brushes, or a water flosser. At Livewell Dental, we review your home-care routine and monitor the implant, gums, bite, and restoration during follow-up visits.

How much will my dental implant treatment cost?

Your cost depends on the number of teeth being replaced, the restoration, and whether you need extractions or bone grafting. Ask Livewell Dental for an itemized estimate covering the implant, abutment, final teeth, and any additional treatment. Our team can discuss payment options and any applicable insurance benefits.

# Smile Makeovers in Mantua, VA


Serving Mantua, VA — a short drive from our Fairfax Station office.

Natural results designed around your face

Preview your smile before you commit

Planned by Dr. Chris and crafted with experienced ceramists


## Because Sometimes, “Good Enough” Isn’t Enough


A small touch-up may not be enough when what you really want is a turning point. Whether it is a wedding, a career-defining presentation, a milestone birthday, a reunion, or simply the everyday confidence of liking what you see in the mirror, a smile makeover is designed around the moment that matters to you.

A smile makeover isn't a single procedure. It's a complete reimagining of your smile, covering color, shape, bite, and harmony, crafted to look naturally like you, only better.

At Livewell Dental, we combine the art of cosmetic design with the science of restoring function. Whether you've lived with worn, mismatched, missing, or damaged teeth for years, or you've simply never truly loved your smile, we bring every tool, every skill, and every detail to the table.

Start Your Makeover Journey


## When Everything Falls Into Place


Imagine walking into that moment knowing your smile is the last thing you are worried about.


### The Wedding Day


You have planned every detail, and your smile will be part of the photos you keep for life. With one patient at a time care, careful planning, and natural-looking design, we help you feel confident from every angle without looking overdone.


### A Fresh Start


Some smiles need rebuilding, not retouching. Because Dr. Chris is one of the few dentists trained in both advanced cosmetics and complex restorative work, we can take on what you were told was beyond repair — and it will function as well as it looks.


### Work, Meetings and Cameras


A presentation, a promotion, a headshot, or simply a day of back-to-back video calls. If you have been managing your smile in meetings, digital previews let you see the planned result before any treatment begins.


### Reunions & Milestones


High school reunions, milestone birthdays, retirement parties, show up feeling like the best version of yourself. Our planning and technology help us work within your timeline without cutting corners.


### Everyday Joy


Sometimes the “big moment” is simply waking up and liking what you see in the mirror. We design smiles that fit your personality, lifestyle, and long-term health.

Let’s Create Your Moment


## A Complete Transformation, Planned to Perfection


Invisalign / Orthodontics

Custom-made shells bonded to the front of your teeth. They change the shape, shade, and proportion of each tooth individually. At Livewell, every veneer is designed using dentofacial analysis and fabricated by master ceramists who specialize in natural-looking restorations.

learn more

When a tooth needs more than surface-level change, a crown restores its full shape and strength while matching the aesthetics of the surrounding teeth. Often part of a makeover when structural and cosmetic needs overlap.

Professional-grade whitening that goes beyond what strips and trays can reach. Used as a standalone treatment or as a finishing step to match veneers, crowns, or bonding to the brightest natural shade your teeth can achieve.

Composite resin applied directly to the tooth to repair chips, close small gaps, or reshape edges. Conservative, often completed in a single visit, and blended to match the exact shade and texture of your natural teeth.

When too much gum tissue makes teeth look short or uneven, recontouring reshapes the gumline to create symmetry and proportion. The frame matters as much as the teeth inside it.

Alignment correction before or alongside cosmetic work. Straightening your teeth first can reduce the amount of reshaping or bonding needed, which means a more conservative final result.


## Leading You Every Step of the Way


Dr. Chris is a graduate of the UCSF School of Dentistry and its AEGD residency program.

He completed advanced training at the Kois Center, one of the most rigorous postgraduate institutions in comprehensive dentistry, and earned Fellowship in both the Academy of General Dentistry and the International Congress of Oral Implantologists.

His training in cosmetics, restorative dentistry, bite function, and complex treatment planning helps him design smile makeovers that look natural and function comfortably.

DDS, UCSF School of Dentistry (2015)

AEGD Residency, UCSF (2016)

Fellow, Academy of General Dentistry (FAGD)

Graduate, Kois Center (2021)

Fellow, International Congress of Oral Implantologists (FICOI)

MEET DR. CHRIS


## Smile Makeovers, Done the Livewell Way


Your makeover follows a blueprint. Every step is designed, reviewed, and confirmed before anything permanent happens. You will know what your result looks like before we begin.

Discovery and Design

We photograph your face, your teeth, and your smile from every angle that matters. Using dentofacial analysis and digital smile design, Dr. Chris maps the relationship between your teeth, your lips, your jawline, and your facial proportions. The goal is a design that belongs to your face, not a template pulled from a catalog.

Preview You Can Try On

Before any tooth is touched, you see your result. A physical preview is built so you can wear your new smile temporarily, check it in different lighting, and decide whether it feels right. If something needs to change, it changes now, not after the final restorations are placed.

Preparation

Once the design is locked, the teeth are prepared. For veneers, this means minimal reshaping of the front surface. For crowns, a more complete reduction. For bonding, often no preparation at all. The approach depends on the tooth and the restoration, not a standard formula.

Handcrafted Fabrication

Your restorations are built by experienced ceramists who receive the full photography package, digital design, and specific shade instructions captured with PolarEyes. The goal is a close partnership where the ceramist understands the same details Dr. Chris sees.

Delivery and Final Verification

Each restoration is tried in, checked against the original design, and verified for shade, fit, and bite before it is permanently bonded. We photograph the final result and compare it to the plan. What you approved is what you get.


## Where Advanced Training Meets Artistry


Beautiful, natural-looking results come from more than technique. Dr. Chris's training at the Kois Center and his close work with a master ceramist mean every veneer and cosmetic restoration is shaped around your face, your bite, and the way you want to feel when you smile.


## The Livewell Smile Makeover Experience


Your makeover is not just a set of procedures. It is an experience designed to feel comfortable, personal, and carefully planned. This is where science, artistry, and one-on-one care come together.


### Private


One-patient-at-a-time visits allow our team to focus fully on your care.


### Ceramist Partnership


We partner with experienced ceramists so restorations are carefully crafted, not treated like factory-made pieces.


### Technology


Digital previews help you understand the planned result before permanent treatment begins.


### Scheduling


Flexible scheduling supports both time-sensitive events and carefully phased treatment plans.


### Expertise


Experience in implants, full-mouth rehabilitation, and aesthetics helps us manage complex smile transformations under one roof.


## The Livewell Smile Collection


Designed with Purpose. Crafted to Belong.


### Perfect 1


One tooth. Perfectly matched. A single restoration (veneer, crown, or bonding) crafted to vanish into your natural smile with microscopic precision.


### Magic 4


Four front teeth. One magical transformation. Ideal for fixing wear, discoloration, or imbalance in the most visible zone of your smile.


### Social 10


Ten upper teeth, harmonized to perfection. Balanced, bright, and confident — ready for any setting, any angle, any moment.


## Watch Dr. Chris explain the Livewell lab partnership


Watch Now

"The most important thing in dentistry happens outside the dental chair."


## Not Rushed. Not Templated. Designed Around You.


Your first visit is not a sales pitch. It is a comprehensive examination with full imaging, clinical photography, and a case presentation where you see everything we see before any recommendation is made. That is the standard for every patient, whether the plan involves one tooth or ten.

One patient at a time. No double-booking, no rotating providers.

Every case documented with photography at every stage, from diagnosis to final result.

Your result previewed and approved before anything permanent begins.

Comfort built into every visit: noise-cancelling headphones, warm blankets, aromatherapy.

Schedule a Consultation


## Why Mantua Patients Choose Their Smile Makeover at Livewell


A few things that are different about planning your makeover here, a short drive from Mantua.

01


### Fast-Track When You Have a Date


A wedding, a reunion, a presentation that matters. Tell us the date at your consultation and we prioritise your case and plan backwards from it, preview appointment included.

02


### Phased Care When You Don't


No deadline, or you would rather stage the investment? We map a clear, milestone-based plan so you can begin when you are ready and stop at any point that makes sense.

03


### Comfort Through Every Visit


Minimally invasive where possible, sedation available when appropriate, and one patient at a time, so a visit that took you a drive to reach never feels rushed.

What is a smile makeover and what does it include?

A smile makeover is a combination of cosmetic dental procedures planned and executed together to transform the appearance of your smile. It can include porcelain veneers, dental crowns, teeth whitening, bonding, gum recontouring, and orthodontic alignment. The specific combination depends on your goals, your facial structure, and the current condition of your teeth. At Livewell, every makeover is designed using photography, digital mapping, and a physical preview before anything permanent begins.

Can I see what my smile will look like before I commit?

Yes. Before any permanent work begins, a physical preview is created so you can wear your new smile temporarily and evaluate it in real life. If the shape, shade, or proportion needs adjusting, those changes happen before anything is finalized. You approve the result before it becomes permanent.

How many visits will a smile makeover take, and how far apart are they?

It depends on the scope. A bonding-only case may be one or two visits. A full veneer case typically runs three to six weeks from preparation to final placement, with a consultation, a design and preview appointment, the preparation visit, and delivery. Multi-phase plans that include orthodontics or gum work run longer. Dr. Chris gives you the full schedule at your consultation, so you know how many trips to plan for before you commit to anything.

Are smile makeovers covered by insurance?

Most dental insurance plans classify smile makeovers as elective cosmetic treatment and do not cover them. However, individual components like crowns may receive partial coverage if they also serve a functional purpose. Our team reviews your benefits before treatment begins and walks you through what, if anything, applies.

What is the difference between Perfect 1, Magic 4, and Social 10?

These describe the scope of the makeover. Perfect 1 focuses on a single tooth, matched perfectly to the surrounding teeth. Magic 4 covers your four front teeth, transforming the center of your smile. Social 10 addresses all ten upper teeth visible when you smile or speak. The right scope depends on your goals and your starting point, which is determined during your consultation.

Where is the practice, and how far is it from Mantua?

Livewell Dental is at 9027 Silverbrook Road, Suite F, Fairfax Station, VA 22039, a short drive south of the City of Fairfax. We see patients from Mantua regularly, and the team is happy to help you pick an appointment time that works around the traffic on your route. Call 703-690-0102 and we will talk it through.
